#3626. How Greg Brockman’s Wife Anna Became a Trump and MAGA Mega-Donor

It was weeks before the election and spirits were low in MAGA’s top ranks. The president’s approval ratings had plunged to historic depths. Polling suggested his endorsement had become an albatross for many of his preferred candidates. And so Donald Trump had retreated to the gilded comfort of Mar-a-Lago to attend to “matters of national importance,” including, on October 17, a candlelit dinner with some of his most loyal supporters.

At the head of the table were just four seats: Google cofounder Sergey Brin, President Trump himself, OpenAI cofounder Greg Brockman, and his wife, Anna Brockman.

Anna Brockman, Greg Brockman, President Donald Trump, and Sergey Brin during a MAGA Inc. event at Mar-a-Lago. October 17, 2026.

The Brockmans, worth nearly $30 billion, have used their wealth to become the 16th-biggest political mega-donors this midterms cycle: Last year, the couple donated a combined $25 million to MAGA Inc. and $25 million to the pro-AI super PAC Leading the Future. Greg has said that he and his wife are “single-issue donors,” their lone cause being AI, the technology he’s helped build. “It’s not popular,” he recently acknowledged, so “we really want to support politicians who really lean into [it].” And it has been “we” at each of these turns—the Brockmans working in tandem toward a shared vision of the future.

Yet despite Anna Brockman’s frequent presence amid the backdrop of this pivotal scene in history, next to nothing has previously been reported about her. When The Wall Street Journal profiled Greg Brockman in May, they wrote of his elusive wife, “She is intensely private: almost no information, including her maiden name, is available online.”

Anna Chang has an unlikely past—one that raises some new questions. How did a onetime registered Democrat and ambitious tech worker who “loves everything that positively changes the world” become the retired wife of one of the wealthiest men on earth, Donald Trump’s frequent guest, and one of the single-largest donors seeking to hasten a future where artificial intelligence is developed with minimal regulatory oversight?

Sources close to the Brockmans and to OpenAI suggested that Anna is no bystander, and is worthy of scrutiny as a significant player herself. “She’s not a silent sidekick to Greg,” says one AI industry insider. “She is a force.”

When Greg and Anna met at a Silicon Valley dinner party in 2018, Greg said they “instantly connected.” She was the daughter of Korean immigrants, and he had a long-standing reverence for Korean culture: He has a black belt in tae kwon do, and even attended Korean summer camp as a teenager, picking up some of the language. They had also both worked at the payments-software start-up Stripe in the 2010s, though their tenures never overlapped. (Both Greg and Anna Brockman declined Vanity Fair’s request for comment for this story.)

In 2015, Greg had left his position as Stripe’s chief technology officer to cofound OpenAI with 10 fellow visionaries out of his San Francisco living room. A gifted and relentless coder, he muscled his way through seemingly impossible projects in the hopes of eventually achieving artificial general intelligence, or AGI (the point when the technology can match or exceed human-level capabilities at every possible task). He sometimes clocked 90-hour workweeks. Greg’s colleagues from over the years describe him as fiercely competitive, not just with work projects but also with hobbies like running and weight lifting.

Anna was a quirky and exuberant animal lover from Texas—one source estimates she and her husband live with over 20 animals—who had worked for AmeriCorps mentoring working-class students after graduating from Wesleyan University, well known as an ultraliberal school. (In a total coincidence, I discovered midway through reporting that Anna and I had overlapped there during our college years.) When she became one of the first 100 or so employees at Dropbox, her idealism persisted. In an introduction to her new colleagues, she told them she spent her free time “taking on adventures to help save the world.”

While a source close to Anna said she doesn’t drink alcohol, sources who’ve spent time with her said she has sometimes drawn attention for her juvenile humor and unconventional manner. She “curses like a drunken sailor,” said one. Another described her as “fratty.”

Early in the Brockmans’ relationship, Anna experienced a series of mysterious health mishaps. The couple spent years visiting doctor after doctor, and eventually discovered she had Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome (hEDS). Greg has also said that she has Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS) and Mast Cell Activation Syndrome (MCAS). She believed that with the right AI tools, her arduous investigation might have been made much simpler. “Her whole passion for AI is driven by this medical journey,” said her friend and former colleague Sujay Jaswa.

In her late 30s, Anna was also diagnosed with autism. “Her autism can come at a cost, one of which is requiring a lot of alone time (the fur kids and myself excluded) and downtime to rest and recover,” her husband wrote, referring to their many pets. “A beautiful trait of her autism is her deep connection to animals and attention to understanding their needs,” Greg posted on X.

He, too, required patience from his partner while he focused on his interior life. During their first holiday season together, he decided to teach himself machine learning, scratching out equations in a notebook. “She was there with me no matter how many planned activities it meant skipping,” he wrote on his blog. He described her as “someone who made me feel it was ok if I failed.” Greg said on the Tetragrammaton With Rick Rubin podcast that they even put off having children so that he could focus all his energy on AI.

Anna’s early adoption of AI tools helped her practically float up the corporate ladder, but it also opened the door to loftier visions. In a 2018 blog post, she wrote, “I believe in the power of AI to allow us to become more human, today and in the future, by alleviating monotony and opening the space for creativity and intuition.”

Meanwhile, Greg sounded like he was experiencing vertigo from the progress they were making at OpenAI. His journals from this period, portions of which were later made public as part of discovery for the Musk v. Altman trial, ricochet between self-doubt and megalomania. “No person should have control over what we’re creating,” he wrote in August 2017. Then three months later, he appeared to copy and paste a chat with an unknown correspondent into the journal document. “It is better for us to become increasingly kings of this industry,” one of them wrote. “Being the kings of AI is not so bad.”

In Anna, he found the ultimate support system. According to the WSJ, he took the other side of a bet with his then OpenAI colleague (and later Anthropic cofounder) Daniela Amodei, who wagered $100 that Anna was not the one. He won. As Greg put it, they “have been inseparable ever since.”

At the Musk v. Altman trial, Anna was by her husband’s side almost every day. Some observers noted that she held his hand right up to the last second as she walked him to the witness stand. Sources who know the couple described Anna, 38, as “very devoted” and Greg, 38, as “the ultimate wife guy.”

When Anna and Greg got married in 2019, they held a civil ceremony in OpenAI’s office officiated by fellow OpenAI cofounder Ilya Sutskever. The ring bearer was a robotic hand.

As wife to the “wife guy” at the helm of one of the most powerful companies on earth, Anna has enjoyed a front row seat to scenes of such intrigue that they have inspired multiple books, and the highly anticipated upcoming film Artificial. (Cooper Hoffman, the actor who plays Brockman in the film Artificial, recalls director Luca Guadagnino’s guidance on how to approach the role: “Greg is all-American,” Guadagnino told him. “He’s like a cheeseburger.”)

The Brockmans attended the Met Gala in 2025.

While it isn’t uncommon for spouses and partners to turn up in the offices of start-ups, sources who’ve spent time with the Brockmans noted that by the late 2010s Anna was unusually engaged in his work life, having left her own job at the venture capital firm Basis Set Ventures. While, per The Information, Anna has never been formally employed at OpenAI, over the years she has appeared in live product demos; accompanied executives on trips, like one to South Korea to meet with local start-ups; and even been spotted at high-level meetings at the OpenAI office.

When OpenAI’s top executives were appointed drivers and private security, Anna would sometimes be spotted in the car with Greg, taking him to work, according to former colleagues.

As the money piled up, the relationships between the company’s early team—including Sam Altman, Greg Brockman, Ilya Sutskever, Jakub Pachocki, Mira Murati, and Dario and Daniela Amodei—began to fray. While the imaginations of many of their Bay Area peers ran wild with sci-fi visions of uploaded consciousness and unfathomable abundance, and AI doomsayers warned of extinction events, the Brockmans’ hopes for an AI future felt relatively pedestrian.

Greg was firmly in the pro-commercialization camp, according to OpenAI researchers who’ve worked with him, believing that above all, AI can empower individuals to transform their own lives. Anna, meanwhile, is driven by the “idea that AI for all is gonna take all these major social problems, like the extreme cost of health care and education [and] extreme inequality in access…and it’s gonna democratize all of it,” according to Jaswa.

And to do that, the Brockmans understood that AI leaders needed to win over the policymakers that, in their view, could stand in the way of AGI.

Following the release of ChatGPT in 2022, OpenAI’s founding team found themselves on the other side of overnight fame—at least in the insular tech bubble of the Bay Area. While some of the more socially awkward researchers chafed at the attention, Greg—who’d been promoted to president of the company—and Anna have seemed to bask in it.

The Brockmans have dined with Sylvester Stallone at the Kennedy Center, attended black-tie events at the White House, and even walked the blue carpet at the Met Gala, where Anna wore a black-and-white ruffled gown by Korean designer Ashlynn Park.

The power she’d been quietly amassing by Greg’s side played out in a more significant and dramatic way in November 2023, when the board of OpenAI removed Sam Altman from his position as CEO over concerns that he was untrustworthy. Sutskever, who was on the board, also compiled a memo detailing allegations against Greg, and Greg was removed from his position as chairman of the board (but allowed to stay on as president). When the board called Greg to inform him of their decision, the first thing he did was talk to his wife. He told her, “‘We have to leave.’ And she said, ‘Yes, we do,’” he said on the Tetragrammaton With Rick Rubin podcast. He warned her they would have to be prepared for his equity to disappear if he quit. “‘Still want to do it?’ And she said yes.”

But when the board began to reconsider its decision, Sutskever became the deciding vote. In an oft-repeated piece of OpenAI lore, Anna allegedly begged Sutskever in a tearful encounter to reconsider. (Sources familiar with the events have suggested that the impact of this encounter has been overstated.) According to the WSJ, when Sutskever decided to reverse his decision, Anna left him a cactus as a gift.

After a long negotiation over his place at the company, Sutskever left to start his own venture, Safe Superintelligence. “There were some deep and bitter things” that went down during this period, according to one high-level employee at the time.

After this dramatic inflection point, which has come to be known as the blip, Greg took a three-month leave of absence. This period allowed him to dedicate himself to a project he was passionate about: developing a biological foundation model for genome modeling and design at the Arc Institute—“a domain that’s very personally meaningful to both me and and to my wife,” he has said.

Meanwhile, the company had replaced nearly all the board members who’d risen up against Altman with what one former senior OpenAI employee called a “more loyal and ‘normie’” board who were supportive of the company’s commercial push.

The center of gravity began to shift in Greg’s direction, solidifying his place as Altman’s second in command, soon to be tasked with an even more fraught assignment: building political goodwill. What wouldn’t the billionaire couple do to help the technology that they consider vital to humanity’s future?

“He thinks big, but he is also very practical, kind of a realist,” Peter Welinder, OpenAI’s vice president and general manager, says of Greg. Others felt that his techno-optimism, and subsequent push into Washington to defend those ideals, is “naivete,” says the former high-level employee. “I don’t think he’s very carefully thinking through the political and power implications.”

When Donald Trump was reelected in late 2024, OpenAI found itself facing down a new threat. Elon Musk, an original cofounder of the company who left in 2018, had grown increasingly antagonistic toward his onetime colleagues while also growing close to the incoming administration. According to Kevin Roose’s The AGI Chronicles, OpenAI, and Altman in particular, feared political retribution from Musk, who now had his own competitor company in xAI, if he was allowed to take up all the oxygen in Washington. At the same time, OpenAI’s need for energy and compute had grown so insatiable that the company had no choice but to seek the government’s help. In an administration run on quid pro quo, OpenAI would have to make nice.

Brockman found himself uniquely well-positioned to lead the infrastructure-scaling bonanza, thanks to a preexisting relationship with Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum, who hailed from his home state of North Dakota. Greg was also “the most credible” face of the political donations, said one former OpenAI employee.

And so Greg and Anna Brockman became White House mainstays. They have attended state dinners for foreign leaders like Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman and Xi Jinping, and joined top tech executives at a White House event about the future of AI. Brockman, rather than Altman, flanked Trump during the signing of the White House Accord on Super Intelligence in September.

When the political pendulum began to swing back this summer, it began to appear as though whoever had made the call on those political donations might have made a severe miscalculation. Following a steady drumbeat of negative headlines about Leading the Future’s work and significant internal dissent among OpenAI employees, the Brockmans rescinded their second planned $25 million donation to the PAC. Greg wrote in a Slack message, obtained by The New York Times, that Leading the Future had become a “distraction” from OpenAI’s work.

When I reached out to OpenAI to discuss the Brockmans’ political giving, it directed me back to the Brockmans’ team. In an interview this October with Vanity Fair’s global editorial director Mark Guiducci, Altman said, “I did not ask him to donate or stop donating. He can make his own personal decision.” It seems the Brockmans’ donations are a hot potato no one is eager to catch.

Regardless, their $25 million checks have helped provide the funds to enable a torrent of preelection ads, including warnings like, “This is the final battle” to “liberate America from these villains, once and for all.”

Some observers of the company have come to believe that the plan was “to have Greg be the scapegoat if/when the Democrats come back into power, but to allow OpenAI to privately (with the White House) claim credit for the MAGA PAC donations with the Trump administration while privately (with employees) distance itself from them,” according to the former senior employee. (OpenAI did not respond to a request for comment.)

Meanwhile, Greg has returned more of his focus to the product realm, and he and his wife have found a less controversial way to spend their millions. When the couple found out that the Big Bear Valley habitat of two publicly beloved eagles, Jackie and Shadow, was under threat, they donated over $5.5 million to preserve the land this summer. “[Jackie and Shadow] inspire perseverance and a sense of connectedness to something greater,” Anna said of their donation.

“It was clear in talking to her that she loved her husband very much and that she loved the eagles,” says Jenny Voisard, the communications and PR leader for Friends of Big Bear Valley, of her experience working with Anna on the donation. They never talked about politics.

#3625. GTA 6 Worldwide Release Times Revealed, And The US Gets It Almost Last

GTA 6 is one of the most-anticipated games ever, and it arrives on November 19. People naturally want to know when exactly that day it will be available to play, and now Rockstar has confirmed the details.

The game will launch at midnight local time on November 19 "in all regions" across PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Given that, it seems the US will be among the last major markets to get it.

The regional release rollout means people in New Zealand and Australia will get in first and the US will be among the final major regions to get started.

In short, GTA 6 will become available to play in New Zealand at midnight in the country, which works out to 5 AM PT / 8 AM ET on November 18. People in the US will then have to wait 16 hours to play GTA 6 where they live.

Given this, people in the US will be in for a tough day as they see the game go live for other people and have to wait. If you're concerned about spoilers, that's another reason to be on guard that day.

While GTA 6 unlocks on November 19, preloading for the 212GB game begins on November 10 for digital copies and November 12 for the code-in-a-box versions sold at retailers.

According to SensorTower, GTA 6 has already sold close to 7 million copies via preorders, and that number could climb to 25 million by launch. That would work out to more than $2 billion in revenue, which is reportedly enough to pay for the game's development budget.

Disney has always been known for its animated blockbusters, but Frozen (which is streaming with a Disney+ subscription) became a full-blown sensation upon its release in 2013. Its sequel Frozen II crushed at the box office, and two more sequels were quickly announced. Although the studios' Head of Animation recently revealed a big change coming to the next two installments of the franchisee

The first Frozen III footage debuted at D23 over the summer, so anticipation for the threequel is steadily building. While we'll have to wait another year until it arrives in November of 2027, Disney's Jared Bush spoke to Collider about how the studio is approaching the next two movies. He revealed that they're putting a full emphasis on the third movie, rather than trying to put out 3 and 4 in quick succession. In his words:

Looking at Frozen 3 and what a Frozen 4 could look like, I know early on it was, 'We're going to put them right together, and they're going to be out in the world. It's going to happen quick.' That's not what we're doing, for a lot of reasons.

Rather than trying to produce a third and fourth Frozen movie as a cash grab (although they're sure to rake in the bucks), it sounds like the powers that be at Disney are putting story first. This is sure to be a relief for fans who might be worried about the property's legacy being soiled by the next two installments.

Fans are excited for Anna and Kristoff's wedding in the threequel, and to reportedly see Olaf get a love interest. Although we shouldn't expect Frozen III to do a bunch of set up for the developing fourth movie. As Bush went on to say:

To me, an important one is we want to make sure that Frozen 3 is the best movie it can possibly be, so that when you get to the end of the movie, do you feel like you've watched a complete story? That it feels like something that feels fulfilling. That doesn't always mean that everything is buttoned up, but it does mean that you have to be building to something that feels worthy of the end of a franchise that's that important to people.

Honestly, I love this strategy. Rather than getting too big picture about the Frozen franchise as a whole, it sounds like the next two installments will tell independent, fully formed stories. So we shouldn't expect any MCU-esque credits scene that help to set up the fourth movie once Frozen III hits theaters next year.

Sometimes thinking too far ahead can frustrate moviegoers when it comes to franchise films. For instance, Halloween Kills got some backlash upon its release for keeping Jamie Lee Curtis' Laurie Strode in the background and set up her role in the threequel. Luckily the third Frozen movie won't be doing that, and will instead tell its own complete narrative.

All will be revealed when Frozen III hits theaters November 24th, 2027. Since its not on the 2026 movie release list, we'll have to practice patience until footage get its wide release.

#3623. Kristen Bell and Dax Shepard's Most Polarizing Comments Over the Years

Kristen Bell and Dax Shepard have become some people’s favorite couple in Hollywood, but others scrutinize their every move.

Bell started dating Shepard in 2007. The couple got engaged in 2009, eventually tying the knot in 2013. Bell and Shepard went on to welcome daughters Lincoln (born in March 2013) and Delta (born in December 2014).

While their relationship has made headlines since the start, Shepard’s popular podcast, “Armchair Expert,” and Bell’s success on Netflix’s Nobody Wants has put even more attention on the pair.

“Having someone I feel that is very opposite from me is certainly something that I feel. I feel like my real-life husband and I are ‘opposites attract,'” she told People while comparing her onscreen romance with Adam Brody to her real-like marriage ahead of the release of season 2 in October 2025. “But that doesn’t mean we couldn’t make it work, or didn’t want to make it work.”

Keep scrolling for a full breakdown on why people can’t stop talking about Bell and Shepard:

In 2021, Shepard and Bell made major headlines for sharing their showering habits.

The couple admitted to only giving their daughters showers when they start to “stink” during an interview on The View at the time. Shepard and Bell said they used to give their girls a bath “every single night before bed,” but things changed as they got older.

“Once you catch a whiff, that’s biology’s way of letting you know you need to clean it up,” Bell said, noting that they sometimes would go “five or six days” without washing the girls. “There’s a red flag, because honestly, it’s just bacteria. And once you get the bacteria, you gotta be like, ‘Get in the tub or the shower.’”

Months after the shower admission, Bell and Shepard got real about how they speak with their daughters about sex.

“The woman takes the man’s penis and puts it in her vagina,” he said during a 2021 “Armchair Expert” episode. “Right away it’s like, you’re in charge of this and you will decide to put this in your vagina. Not the man puts his penis in your vagina.”

He said it was a “nice little adjustment” they made to discuss consent with their kids.

Bell made headlines in September 2024 when she admitted to letting her daughters roam free during a family trip to Denmark.

“The hack is when we went to Copenhagen, we stayed at this hotel that was right at Tivoli Gardens, which is like a 7-acre theme park. It’s an old one,” she said on Jimmy Kimmel Live!. “The hotel opens up into the theme park and so we just were kind of like, ‘Are we going to free-range parenting and roll the die here?’ They woke up at, like, 6 every morning. They scanned their bracelets to go outside. [We] didn’t see them for seven hours. Just running around Copenhagen.”

She said it was “heaven” for her and Shepard.

“We just had coffee. We played Spades, and then around 3, we’d be like, ‘Anybody see them?’” she recalled. “And then one of them would run up and need a Band-Aid or whatever.”

Over the years, Shepard has not been shy when it comes to showing off his wife.

In May 2021, he made headlines for sharing a photo of Bell doing naked yoga to celebrate Mother’s Day.

“Mom’ing has changed since I was a kid … and I’m here for it. Look at this specimen: kind, patient, nurturing, hilarious, Uber talented, generous, hard AND soft,” he captioned the since-deleted Instagram post. “My girls and I hit the MegaMom Lottery. We are so grateful and so in love with you.”

Years later, he gave social media followers more than they bargained for after Bell was nominated for a 2025 Emmy Award. He posted a photo of Bell’s butt up in the air — but it was blurred out for the folks at home.

“People might not know everything that happens behind the scenes in order to create an Emmy nominated performance like Kristen’s,” he captioned the photo. “This may or may not have been a part of her training, but it felt right. CONGRATULATIONS!!!!!”

Bell shared a controversial post when celebrating her and Shepard’s 12th anniversary in October 2025.

“Happy 12th wedding anniversary to the man who once said to me: ‘I would never kill you,” she captioned the post. “A lot of men have killed their wives at a certain point. Even though I’m heavily incentivized to kill you, I never would.’”

Instagram users called out Bell for writing that caption during Domestic Violence Awareness. The National Network to End Domestic Violence shared a statement to Page Six amid the controversy.

“There’s nothing funny about domestic violence ‘jokes’ that trivialize the very real fear, trauma and pain that millions of victims and survivors face each day,” they shared. “Especially during Domestic Violence Awareness Month, we all have a responsibility to support victims and survivors, to invest in proven solutions and to speak about this issue with the seriousness it deserves.”

After the anniversary post, a video of them from 2012 resurfaced where Shepard made an off-color joke about “hitting” Bell. The two were discussing riding in a car he worked on with Bell in the passenger seat.

“He was so excited. We drove to brunch and the first thing I said, five minutes into the ride, I said, ‘This sounds like it’s gonna break,’” she said, recalling that Shepard was “very offended” by her reaction.

“And then I hit her several times,” Shepard replied, joking. Bell responded, “And then I got beat up, and guess what — I never opened my mouth again.”

During an October 2026 episode of Shepard’s “Armchair Expert” podcast featuring guests Bell, Justine Lupe, Timothy Simons and Adam Brody, the Frozen star revealed that her husband flirts with her by complimenting other people.

“If we go to a dinner or something, like, there’s a couple things Dax does where he doesn’t have to look up and wink at me, but I know that he’s just being the best boy,” she said. “We’ll be at dinner, and, like, he’ll say to the waiter or waitress, he’ll go, ‘Wow, you have incredible eyelashes, gorgeous eyes, great job.'”

When Shepard’s cohost, Monica Padman, pointed out that this is a form of flirting with other women, Bell responded, “But that’s flirting with me, because he just made someone else feel good.”

“‘Cause he’s gonna have zero interaction with — let’s say it is a girl. He’s gonna have zero interaction with this girl for the rest of his life. The chances of him ever having another conversation with her are so microscopic,” she continued. “But to me, to know that my partner actively smiles at people and gives them compliments [makes me feel good].”

Bell also said that Shepard has never crossed the line and gone too far with his compliments.

“You’ve never done anything that’s felt even borderline … you, like, you’ll point out someone has great eyebrows, or great cheekbones,” she said.

“That’s why it makes me fluttery inside. That’s why it gives me butterflies,” Bell noted. “Because everyone saw it, he’s the only one that said it, maybe she hadn’t had a compliment today. And I’m with the guy that’s pouring compliments on people? Making people feel good?”

The revelation stirred up controversy as fans questioned whether this is respectful behavior in a relationship.

#3622. The Elder Scrolls 6 Is Officially Titled Sentinel

Confirming a recent report, Bethesda has confirmed the subtitle of the next Elder Scrolls game as The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. This was shared as part of a 40-year-anniversary video recapping many of Bethesda's highlights over the year.

Unfortunately, that's all that was shared about the game, though we did get a (very familiar-looking) title card showing the game's name in the classic Elder Scrolls font. Bethesda subsequently shared a video with a scroll emerging from the sand, which you can see below.

The one hint of what might await in the game was a quote that follows the name reveal. It's attributed to Yazar, Moth Priest of High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell in 4E 206: "The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes. A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate."

Two details stick out there: the reference to a scroll and Hammerfell. A recent report from The Verge stated that Elder Scrolls VI will be set in Hammerfell and focus on the history of the titular Elder Scrolls and discovering their secrets. A follow-up tweet from Bethesda states that the game's location has been revealed, so it seems we are indeed headed to Hammerfell.

More notably, Bethesda says it'll "be some time" before more is shared, so don't expect this announcement to signal the beginning of a proper marketing campaign or anything of the sort.

The Elder Scrolls VI was announced way back in 2018, at a time that Bethesda boss Todd Howard later admitted was not his preference. Virtually nothing has been shared about the game since that debut trailer, including any imagery, hence the reason we've all seen that mountain range countless times in the eight-plus years since.

Earlier this year, it was revealed that the majority of Bethesda Game Studios staff are at work on the game, with Howard saying, “We know we need to get it right and it’s been a long time." The last core entry in the series, Skyrim, released in 2011, meaning it will be more than a 15-year gap between new games.

No release date or platforms for The Elder Scrolls VI have been announced, although Bethesda's parent company, Xbox, has faced renewed pressure to turn its business around. In part, that will involve focusing on its biggest franchises, with Fallout 5 also in the works, though Bethesda devs are said to fear further layoffs.

#3621. Ta-Nehisi Coates on Haley Stevens, Abdul El-Sayed, and the Right’s “Campaign of Hate”

When Michigan congresswoman Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers yesterday, she offered a curious framing. “I’m choosing country over hate,” Stevens claimed. “This is not anti-Muslim at all.”

Rogers, for his part, invoked Martin Luther King Jr.: “You cannot solve darkness with darkness; you have to solve it with light. You can’t solve hate with hate; you have to solve it with love.” For the site of their hard launch, the odd couple chose Perfecting Church, a Black church in Detroit, evidently seeking to exploit the aura of social justice implicit in the Black faith tradition.

Aura farming aside, it is very hard to square the claims of patriotism and love with the actual campaign that Stevens now supports. Indeed, since the moment Abdul El-Sayed triumphed in the Democratic Senate primary, Rogers has made his views of his opponent clear. “I spent years hunting terrorists and bringing Osama bin Laden to justice,” he claimed the morning after El-Sayed won. “Never in a million years did I think that I would be running against someone who believes America deserved 9/11.” (Never mind that Hasan Piker, not El-Sayed, said the 9/11 quote, which El-Sayed has disavowed.)

Indeed, a consistent theme of Rogers’s campaign has been the implication that El-Sayed is a tool for shadowy forces originating in the East. “The Muslim Brotherhood celebrated exactly one victory in the United States in the primary this year,” Rogers claimed. “Abdul El-Sayed’s.” As a factual matter, the attack is highly dubious. But facts are not the point, so much as the deployment of “Muslim” as a slur.

To understand this, one need only look to the overlord of the Rogers campaign, President Donald Trump. As is his wont, Trump delights in mangling El-Sayed’s name, referring to him as “Abduladadalalalala” or simply “Mohamed.” “Somebody said his name isn’t Mohamed,” Trump told attendees at a rally. “I’m the president, I can call him whatever the hell I want. To me, he’s Mohamed.”

The Trump theory of El-Sayed holds that his ascendance is being facilitated by the machinations of Wayne County, a “strictly Third World” jurisdiction that seeks to elevate to Congress a “jihadist” who shouldn’t even be eligible for “a seat on an airplane.” If seated in the world’s greatest deliberative body, El-Sayed, the theory holds, would execute his dastardly plan to ban Christmas and—you guessed it—impose Sharia law.

Trump’s attacks have been echoed and amplified by right-wing news outlets like Newsmax, which has lambasted El-Sayed as an “anti-Israel Muslim,” an “immigrant from another Muslim country,” and a Midwest variant of that other alien, Zohran Mamdani, the “socialist Muslim who’s always smiling.” For those too dense to catch the message, the Newsmax chyrons have helpfully driven home the point—“THE LEFT IS FORGETTING THE HEINOUS ATTACKS OF 9/11,” “DEMOCRATS DROOL OVER NON-WHITE SOCIALISTS,” “MUSLIMS TELL US THEY’RE TAKING OVER, AND THEY ARE.”

Lest one think that this bigotry is merely limited to the crude ramblings of unlettered ogres, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has stepped in to offer some intellectual heft to the attack. The Muslim Brotherhood, according to Kennedy, is responsible for not just the menace that is El-Sayed, but also the dark age that has fallen over the entirety of the Arabdom. “There’s 500 million Arabs in the world,” Kennedy claimed, “and yet they don’t produce science, they don’t win the Nobel Prize, they don’t win the Field[s] prize, they don’t win the Wolf Prize, they don’t produce the literature they used to produce.”

Again, facts aren’t really the point here, and there is no wisdom in debating a quack whose brain has literally been infected by a worm. Nonetheless, it is worth noting the particular history at work. During both his run for president and his time in the White House, Barack Obama endured his share of racist attacks. To Rush Limbaugh, Obama was “Barack the Magic Negro.” To Newt Gingrich, he was America’s “food stamp president.” At the Value Voters Summit, a vendor hawked “Obama Waffles,” a product featuring a racist caricature of the president on the packaging. The tagline was: “Point box toward Mecca for tastier waffles.” That last line deserves particular attention. Indeed, by 2016, the political scientist Philip Klinkner would find that the best way to discern whom a voter would support in the upcoming election was to pose a simple question—“Is Barack Obama a Muslim?”

Stevens, in joining Rogers, has allied herself with this odious culture war, one that is itself tied to a very real war. The campaign of hate, of which El-Sayed is the latest victim, has a simple goal: to render Muslims and Arabs more killable. The latter does not require the former. In 1953 the CIA backed a coup that overthrew a democracy in Iran. In 1965 it supported a coup in Indonesia, the country with the largest Muslim population in the world, that killed between 500,000 and a million people. During the Cold War, the justification for this death toll was the threat of communism; post-9/11, it is racism. In 2008, John McCain confronted a supporter and disputed the claim that Obama was Arab. “No, ma’am,” McCain told his supporter. “He’s a decent family man.” This moment is often referenced as an act of patriotism, and perhaps it was one. But the notion that “decent” people exist in one place, while Arabs exist in another, is the major premise for a syllogism of violent, chauvinist power—wedding parties droned, governments overthrown, schoolgirls bombed, and inconvenient people eliminated.

This long war on the Muslim and Arab world has reached its apogee in the concentration camp of Gaza, where every single bomb was dropped from a plane of American extraction. And the genocide is but the latest chapter in a book authored by Israel, a state whose own basic laws reserve full rights for its “decent” people and something less for everyone else. This is the state that Haley Stevens has claimed to literally see in her dreams. And it is ultimately the defense of this state that drove Stevens into the arms of Mike Rogers. From this perspective, Stevens’s defection isn’t a story about party intrigue. It is a story about Stevens waking up and choosing violence.

#3620. What to Wear When Exercising Outdoors, Based on How Cold It Is

I fell in love with cold weather running while I was training for a spring marathon. It wasn’t a choice at first: Some weeks, the weather was bad for days on end, and if I stayed home, I would fall behind in my training. Everybody else in my training group was braving the elements, so I did too—with no regrets.

I got to run on quiet mornings while snow was softly falling. I signed up for a winter race that herded finishers into a heated barn for hot chocolate and soup. I set a personal record at a spring race, during which I pushed myself hard without breaking a sweat. I now find it sad when somebody tells me they’re afraid of running in the cold, or that they would run in the winter but don’t know what to wear.

No, cold weather doesn’t have to stop you from running, but getting dressed can be a puzzle: How do you keep from freezing your butt off at first and avoid overheating once you start to sweat? Fortunately, it isn’t as tough as it looks. With the right gear, your fingers and ears can stay toasty while you jog through a winter wonderland. Below, I’ll give you a temperature-by-temperature running cheat sheet, and then dive into the specifics on how to buy the best socks, shirts, and more.

When I get dressed to run in winter, I take a look at the “feels like” temperature, not the actual high or low. I also make sure to check the weather for the time I’ll go running, not for the whole day. It doesn’t matter how warm it will be at 2 p.m. if my run will be happening at 6 a.m., before the sun is up. I use the Carrot Weather app, but any app that gives you hourly feels-like temps will work just fine.

Next, use the 20-degree rule. Imagine that the temperature is 20 degrees (Fahrenheit) warmer than it really is. What would you wear then? Here's an example: if it’s 50 degrees out, you should dress as if it were 70: in a T-shirt and shorts, most likely. If it’s 30 degrees, you’d dress as if it were 50: long pants and maybe a light jacket. Get the idea?

Everybody has their own preferences. Some people wear shorts even when it’s snowing, while others will pop a beanie on as soon as there’s a detectable chill in the air. I’m a pretty middle-of-the-road runner when it comes to keeping warm, so here’s what I wear at each “feels like” temperature, starting with warmer weather and working our way colder. I'll give a guide to each type of garment or accessory at the end.

At 50+ degrees Fahrenheit, I’m wearing basically the same things I would for a summer run.

Head and hands: Nothing special. No gloves and no hat, unless it’s a baseball cap to shade my eyes from the sun.

We’re starting to feel the first bit of a chill. This is where I may start bringing gloves, although they’ll probably get stuffed into a pocket by the end of the run. Remember, with the 20-degree rule, it will feel like 60 degrees by the time you're warmed up.

Bottoms: Leggings, lightweight long pants, or shorts.

Top: Something with long sleeves, but ideally made of thin material (think long-sleeved T-shirt, not a full-on sweatshirt or jacket). If you wore a sun shirt in the summer, that's a good layering option for these cool temps. I like my REI Sahara Shade hoodie here, but any long sleeve will do. If you run fall and winter races, you'll probably be handed a free long-sleeved version at some point.

Hands: I usually just pull my shirt's sleeves over my hands, but you could wear knit gloves if you want. Consider something like Flipmits for an intermediate option (they can be folded down into a wrist cuff when your hands warm up).

Head: A headband if you need protection for your ears.

You may see a few snowflakes drifting down, but don’t bundle up in a snowsuit. Once you’re warmed up, it will only feel like 50 degrees—so go for something in “light jacket” territory.

Bottoms: Leggings or running tights. The fleece-lined kind can be nice. (I have these.)

Top: You’ll want some kind of jacket or sweatshirt. A lightweight, reflective rain jacket is great here, or just throw on a regular hoodie over your T-shirt. (I go with cotton sweats in dry weather or light snow, but I'd go for synthetics or wool if there's rain or sleet.)

Hands: Definitely wear gloves. The cheap knit ones are usually good enough, but consider treating yourself to a nice pair of running gloves.

Head: Your choice of hat or headband; I’d stick with the headband.

Feet: This is around the temperature you may start to want warmer socks. That goes double if snow is in play: snow that falls onto your shoes will work its way through the mesh, melt, and make your feet wet. Wool is a good material here, so consider something like these from Smartwool.

This is where I’ll officially say it’s “cold.” Whatever warm-weather gear you were getting away with at warmer temps, you’ll probably have to swap it out now. Shorts people will break out their long pants. Headband people will wear a real hat.

Bottoms: Leggings and shorts. I don’t care if you think it looks goofy to wear both; this is an A+ hack. Or try a puffer skirt.

Top: It’s definitely jacket weather. Rather than getting a warmer jacket, I like to wear the same light jacket as I did at 30 degrees, but this time with a long-sleeved fleece or wool base layer underneath.

Hands: Real gloves, please. You can keep wearing your little knit gloves if you’re able to tuck your hands inside your jacket sleeves, or if you have a pair of mittens to wear over top; otherwise, get windproof gloves.

Head: A hat, and maybe also a buff for your nose and mouth. (If you have any cloth masks still hanging around from the early COVID days, they’re perfect for cold weather runs.)

Feet: Warm socks for sure. If you’ll be doing a lot of running in these temperatures, you may want shoes that are specialized for the elements. Look for ones with Gore-Tex uppers, like the Brooks Ghost GTX.

This is where I tap out. If a run is just barely in the teens, I’ll make do with the 20-degree items I mentioned above, adding an extra layer wherever needed. But if that isn't enough, I opt for the treadmill. You certainly can run in this weather if you are determined. You’ll want windproof everything, some kind of face covering, and you may need eye protection such as goggles.

Whenever the weather gets to your own personal “too cold” temperature, remember that you still have options. The early afternoon is often the warmest part of the day, so a run may be tolerable then. There’s also no shame in using a treadmill (even if you have to join a cheap gym for this reason alone).

Everybody has different preferences, and with practice you’ll figure out if you’re the kind of person who wears three shirts before it hits freezing or the type to run through the snow in shorts. But this should give you a starting point when you head out for your first (or next) cold weather run.

As you continue on your cold-weather running journey, you may need to buy some new gear or repurpose things from elsewhere in your closet. And yes, the first few minutes of your run will feel chilly. But if you’re wearing the right shoes and clothes (and planning routes with a few extra factors in mind, which I’ll discuss below), winter running is not just feasible; it’s actually fun. So here are the items you may want to consider.

Your feet need to be warm and, if possible, dry. Warm socks go without saying, but there are some extra considerations when you’re picking socks to run in. Wool socks are ideal because they keep your feet warm even when they get wet. You may not think of winter as a wet time, but any snow that meets up with your body heat will turn into water. If you don’t have wool socks, synthetic wicking fabrics are a good second choice. Cotton is a no-no

First, the socks have to be able to fit into your shoes. If you’ve been running in super thin cotton or synthetic socks all summer, thick socks may not fit. Smartwool run socks are available in a thin version that can fit no problem—but in colder weather you’ll want some thickness for extra warmth. That thickness, in turn, may mean that your winter running shoes need to be roomier than the shoes you wear in summer. If you’re buying a new pair, make sure to try them on with the type of socks you intend to run in.

If your warm socks fit, you can make do with the same shoes you wore in the summer. Your feet will stay dry if the weather is dry and you stay out of puddles. If you encounter snow and slush, though, your feet will have to endure warm-but-wet conditions for the rest of your run. That can be okay for short runs, but for serious winter running, consider upgrading your shoes.

Some running shoes are available with water-resistant uppers. This level of water resistance will keep stray snowflakes out of your socks, but it isn’t reliable if you’ll be stepping in slush puddles. In that case, you’ll want something more waterproof, like Gore-Tex shoes, many of which are made for running trails.

If you expect to run on a lot of ice or packed snow, especially on trails, spikes can give you a little extra grip.

Yaktrax makes a rubber harness that stretches to fit your shoe, with steel coils and small spikes, for about $40.

Microspikes are a notch up from there, costing around $90 for what look like a miniature version of the chains you’d put on car tires.

And if you’re really dedicated—and are seeking a purpose-built pair of snow shoes—you can attach individual spikes: either these traction spikes from IceSpike, or via a DIY approach using sheet metal screws. (There’s a tutorial here.)

The versions that include rubber, like Yaktrax, can wear out quickly on pavement, so it’s best to save these for runs on trails or on unplowed paths. You’ll also want to be careful about the fit. I tried a pair that were similar to Yaktrax, but they were a tad too big. Shortly into my run, I found that the rubber stretched enough to pull the front set of spikes up over the top of my shoe. I've since gotten better-fitting ones, and they work great.

Spikes and specialized shoes help you go more places, in worse weather—but remember that they’re not required to just head out on a chilly day. Regular shoes are fine if the weather is cold but dry, or if you’re willing to put up with a little moisture.

I actually love when the weather gets cold enough that I need a jacket, because then I get to wear something that gives me extra pockets! Stick with thin jackets that have some room inside. By the time temps dip into the 20s or below, you’ll be doing some serious layering: for example, an undershirt, a long-sleeved warm layer, and a jacket. A great option for that warm layer is a wool base layer like this one. (Don’t worry, it’s not itchy.) If you can’t wear wool, a synthetic fleece is a good alternative.

Before you run out to buy all new clothes, experiment with what’s in your closet. Try repurposing a thin sweater, for example. Some people would never wear cotton for running (it can be cold when wet), but I wear it as my undershirt layer and have lived to tell the tale. Just make sure to shower or change after your run, so you aren't sitting around in cold, wet clothes.

The jacket is the most important layer. You can grab a sweatshirt in a pinch, but to be really well-equipped for nasty weather, you’ll want a jacket that is windproof and water-resistant. Jackets made for running are lightweight, for layering. Consider ones that are visible at night, with bright colors and reflective areas, and that come with zippered pockets.

Once it’s too cold for shorts, you’ll want to start layering your bottoms, too. Loose pants let cold air in, which is why leggings or “running tights” like these are standard winter wear for all genders. Running tights come in different thicknesses; go for something fleece-lined for your coldest runs, or layer two pairs.

You need to keep your ears warm, but don’t reach for a winter hat right away: an ear warmer or headband can cover your ears while still letting heat escape from the top of your head. And if anything is falling from the sky (say, snow), a baseball cap will keep it out of your eyes.

Fleece or knit hats are great for cold enough days, of course. The dividing line between earwarmer weather and hat weather is a personal one, and depends on whether you’re overheating. If you’re wearing a hat but sweating into your base layers, the hat is probably overkill.

Gloves, however, are essential. I keep a pair of cheap knit gloves in my jacket pockets, but windy or very cold days call for something stronger. You can layer gloves; I find gloves under mittens work well. You can also get windproof insulated gloves, which are warmer than any number of layers of holey knit gloves.

Your face will freeze on windy or very cold days, so this is where your old stash of pandemic face masks really shines. Consider a balaclava or even a fleece-lined bandana. A neck gaiter stays on better than a scarf if your neck is cold. At this point, every inch of you is covered but your eyes. Sunglasses can take care of that.

#3619. GTA 6 File Size Revealed, And It’s Truly Massive–See How It Compares To Other Huge Games

Ahead of the game's release on November 19, GTA 6's file size has been revealed, and it is massive. Rockstar Games has confirmed that people will need about 212GB of space to install the game.

As announced previously, preloading for GTA 6 begins on November 10, which is good news considering the game is massive in terms of its file size. People will no doubt have to delete other content to fit the game on the PS5 or Xbox Series X|S. This is double the file size of Rockstar's last game, Red Dead Redemption II.

How does GTA 6 file size compare to other games?

Content creator NikTek put together a graphic that shows how GTA 6's file size, 212GB, compares to other big games--and it's the biggest.

As you can see, the next closest is Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War (175GB), followed by Assassin's Creed Valhalla (160GB), Stalker 2 (160GB), and Forza Horizon 6 (156GB).

Everyone expected GTA 6's file size to be gigantic, but now there is a number behind it, and it's one that makes it among the largest games ever in terms of file size. GTA 6's map is three times bigger than Red Dead Redemption 2's, and the game is filled with lots of detail in the vein of that game's horse testicles.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and it's expected to be the biggest game of all time. One report said the game could hit 25 million preorders by launch, generating $2 billion in revenue.

GTA 6 is a strictly single-player game, but it's safe to assume that Rockstar will eventually release a new version of GTA Online. A PC edition, meanwhile, is expected in early 2027.

Hailey Bieber had a big October. She knows it too, posting a full thread to Instagram at the end of the month simply captioned “Thanks October” and featuring her in an angel Halloween costume. But before the Internet got that post, she actually channeled Angelina Jolie in a daring Mr and Mrs. Smith fit. Looks like latex is back in, baby.

You remember the scene. In Mr and Mrs Smith, Jolie’s “Jane Smith” is out on assignment and shows up in a full bondage outfit complete with tall boots, a spandex dress and mesh elbow gloves with confusing purpose. Bieber wore a similar look for Halloween this year, and was photographed by portrait photographer Amber Asaly, who admitted she hasn’t seen the Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt classic. (A classic that might be more infamous for the two getting together and leading to Pitt divorcing Aniston, anyway.)

A post shared by amber asaly (@amberasaly)

Separately, Hailey and Justin Bieber also dressed in couples angel and devil costumes for the popular holiday. It’s her channeling Angelina Jolie that’s really sticking with me, however. That movie and scene were super popular 20 years ago, but it's been a while since I've seen someone create a costume based on it. It was unexpected for the Rhode founder, and a fun movie-oriented fit.

Halloween is a time to play around and take risks, and we saw some cool and outlandish celebrity fashion looks this year. Heidi Klum went as a severed hand. JLo channeled her monster-in-law co-star Jane Fonda and dressed as Barbarella. Zendaya looked so good as Halle Berry some people thought it was a literal throwback photo of Halle Berry. My personal favorite inspiration though? DWTS pro Witney Carson is pregnant, and used her belly to dress as the MCU’s “fat Thor.” Perfection.

Bieber’s been taking risks on the fashion realm lately outside of the week leading up to and encompassing Halloween. She also posed for Brazilian Magazine ICE Lately, showing off her bikini tan line. Outside of the sheer dress she wore to see Wuthering Heights, I do typically think of Bieber as being relatively understated when it comes to her fashion, so it’s nice to see her doing something a little more outside the box. I guess that's EXACTLY what Halloween is for!

#3617. Parents Convicted After They Withheld Food and Beat Their Adopted Kids

A couple in Michigan have been convicted of abusing their adopted and fostered children by withholding food and beating them.

A Clinton County jury found Tamal Flore guilty of six counts of first-degree child abuse, two counts of second-degree child abuse and three counts of third-degree child abuse, while Jerry Flore was found guilty on one count of second-degree child abuse.

Jerry, 61, was acquitted on seven counts of first-degree abuse, as well as two additional counts of second-degree abuse.

Each first-degree count is punishable by up to life in prison, while Tamal, 59, and Jerry could face up to 10 years in prison for the second-degree child abuse charge.

The Michigan Attorney General announced the couple’s convictions in a Friday, October 30, following a six-week trial at the state’s 29th Circuit Court.

The pair were arrested after authorities learned of their mistreatment of children, whom they adopted or fostered beginning in 2007. During the trial, prosecutors argued that Tamal and Jerry took the children in “for financial gain and subjected the children to abuse under the guise of discipline.”

“Tamal and Jerry Flore subjected their foster and adopted children to prolonged, routine and systemic mental and physical abuse all for personal financial gain,” Attorney General Dana Nessel said. “Children who become wards of the state are some of the most vulnerable and they must be protected. Today’s conviction ensures that no other children will be subjected to the Flores’ abuse again. I want to offer my heartfelt thanks to Clinton County Sheriff Sean Dush and the prosecutors in my office for their years of effort towards justice.”

They were accused of abusing seven out of 16 children that they fostered or adopted, according to The Detroit News. The children spoke to investigators and reportedly claimed they had been whipped by belts, beaten with spoons and locked in rooms or the garage for days at a time.

The children also claimed they were occasionally forced to sit and sleep in an area of the kitchen, which was known as “the square,” for several weeks and the couple had them do “strong sitting” exercises as a form of punishment.

Following the trial, Jerry’s attorney David Carter said he and his client were “deeply grateful” for the jury’s time after he was only charged with the lone second-degree child abuse conviction.

“They sat through weeks of highly charged, emotional allegations and did exactly what the law required: they looked for independent, verified proof,” Carter said in a statement to the Lansing State Journal. “By returning ‘not guilty’ verdicts on nearly every single count in this indictment, the jury completely rejected the state’s overreached narrative and the deeply flawed, unverified investigation that built it.”

Tamal and Jerry were initially arrested in 2021 and charged with multiple counts of child abuse. Prosecutors dismissed the case in 2023, citing the need for additional investigation. The couple was charged again in December 2025.

“This has been a long and in-depth investigation and without the help of the Michigan Attorney General’s Office we would not have been able to bring this case to a successful completion,” Clinton County Sheriff Sean Dush said following the verdict.

Tamal and Jerry will be sentenced during a hearing on January 11.

If you or someone you know is experiencing child abuse, call or text Child Help Hotline at 1-800-422-4453.

#3615. Anker’s New Soundcore Space 2 Headphones Are Already 18% Off

Anker released the noise-cancelling Soundcore Space One headphones a few years ago, and while they were a more budget-friendly alternative to premium models from Bose and Sony, their performance and fit still fell short in several areas. The brand’s updated Soundcore Space 2 headphones are a major upgrade across the board: They’re comfier, have better ANC, and are currently 18% off at $106.49 (originally $129.99), a rare price cut for a still-new release from a popular brand.

Battery life is one of the Soundcore Space 2’s most attractive features: They last up to 50 hours with ANC on and 70 hours with ANC off, and a five-minute charge gives you up to four extra hours. The noise cancellation is strong for the price, blocking out lower-frequency sounds well. Comfort is also a major upgrade from its sparser predecessor, with roomier, more plush memory foam earcups and a padded headband. They’re also travel-friendly, as the earcups rotate and fold.

The Soundcore app allows you to customize EQ and sound presets, giving you added flexibility if you don’t like the default tuning. Instead of touch-sensitive panels, these headphones use conventional buttons, which help prevent accidental commands while adjusting the earcups and are easy to operate. Along with supporting Bluetooth 6.1, they also have a wired-cable option, which isn’t always the case with modern wireless headphones. That said, they don’t support USB-C audio.

If you want over-ear noise-canceling headphones that perform well but don’t have $200 to shell out for a more expensive model, the Anker Soundcore Space 2 headphones are a comfortable, effective, and long-lasting alternative that hover around $100 at the current discounted price.

#3613. Even Pierce Brosnan Is “Eagerly” Awaiting News of the Next James Bond

Like the rest of us, Pierce Brosnan has been following the seemingly endless and exhaustive search for the next James Bond. Having played 007 across four films, Brosnan says he admires all the actors in the running, but Callum Turner, who played his angsty Manhattanite son in The Only Living Boy in New York, gets a particularly warm mention. “Callum is someone I’ve worked with, and he’s so strong,” Brosnan tells Vanity Fair. As for Dune director Denis Villeneuve’s vision for the franchise, Brosnan is already sold. “I think we are going to be blown away.”

Away from Hollywood, the Irish actor stars in Burberry’s new holiday campaign, celebrating 170 years of the luxury fashion house, alongside actor Fiona Shaw, his son Dylan Thomas Brosnan, and a cast of characters including Dwyane Wade, Cara Delevingne, Gabrielle Union, Nico Parker, and more. Set at the cinematic Longleat House in Wiltshire, England, it’s a festive British Christmas, complete with Burberry’s signature checks and partygoers draped in classic garments. On set, Brosnan found a kindred spirit in Shaw. The two bonded over their shared love of art—though he wishes they had much more time to chat, “It was all too brief with Fiona,” he muses.

Pierce Brosnan in the Burberry Festive 2026 Campaign video.

Pierce Brosnan and Fiona Shaw in the Burberry Festive 2026 Campaign video.

Brosnan is no stranger to good style. Having spent a career playing some of the most impeccably dressed men on screen, from James Bond to Thomas Crown, Brosnan has come to re-embrace the joys of good tailoring after an era of rebelling against the gentlemanly image he created for himself. Now, he’s looking forward to seeing a new generation of leading men step into some of those familiar roles, including Michael B. Jordan, whose upcoming take on Thomas Crown he’s cheering on.

In conversation with Vanity Fair, the former 007 talks favorite Christmas traditions, the Burberry Mac he’s kept for years, the art of playing it cool, how filming MobLand shaped his personal style, and the paintings waiting for him in London.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Vanity Fair: The new Burberry campaign celebrates 170 years of the fashion house with a festive Christmas party in the English countryside. How was your time on the campaign set?

Pierce Brosnan: I was with my son, Dylan Thomas Brosnan, which was just absolutely wonderful, and we had the most magnificent time. I’d never seen so many people on a set in all my days for such an event. Everybody was very charming.

Do you typically go all-in on Christmas? What’s your favorite holiday tradition?

I think it starts with the Christmas tree, and my wife really decks the halls, as it were. She loves decorating the tree, and that becomes a great ritual. The boys are much older now, but we do have grandchildren joining us for Christmas. My son Sean Brosnan and his family will be coming down. My wife is a wonderful cook; she’ll make a feast for us all.

Midnight Mass is a tradition and a great joy if we’re in London. Friends, family, and reflection on the year past. Having been brought up within the Catholic religion, the season and all of those traditions are very much ingrained in me.

Harmony Korine (Gummo, Kids, Spring Breakers) directing a holiday campaign feels like such an inspired choice, given how experimental his films can be. What was it like working with him?

I thought he was charming! Very charming. It moved very fast. He was busy and deep in the workload of the day. The highlight was meeting and being with Fiona Shaw. That was just absolutely magnificent. I’m such a huge fan of the lady’s work.

The Burberry trench is such a cornerstone of British style. Is there a clothing item in your wardrobe that holds that kind of status for you?

Oh, dear. There are so many beautiful items in my closet. One of my favorite suits has become a workhorse because it’s so durable. The cloth is wool, and it’s just a two-piece, beautifully tailored suit by Anglo-Italian. I’m very partial to my shoes and belts by Bottega Veneta. And of course, a Burberry Mac, which I’ve had for many, many years. It is the classic, dream trench coat of anyone who has grown up on the movies.

It was wonderful to celebrate such a garment of classic time, and to be in the company of Fiona Shaw. [She’s] someone who I would adore to work with again on any level, really. We had a wonderful time talking about art. We’re both painters, and art is very much part of the tapestry of our lives now.

Pierce Brosnan in The Thomas Crown Affair, 1999.

Speaking of art, I wanted to ask you about playing Thomas Crown in The Thomas Crown Affair. Michael B. Jordan is stepping into that role now, in a new version of the film, which he’s also directing.

I love Michael B. Jordan. I think he’s an outstanding actor and artist, and I wish him every great success with his vision of Thomas Crown. There’s something just beautifully cinematic about the character. He was brought onto the stage by one of the great actors, Steve McQueen, who was so gifted in the art of film acting, stillness, and inner life. For me, the romance with the film came from his body of work as an actor and has always been with me since I was a young lad in Ireland. These characters are very hard to really understand, but they create a sensation.

He was so cool, Steve McQueen. How do you play cool? You play it with sincerity. You play it with stillness, with just the knowingness—and hopefully some humanity and humility, and a kind of inner knowing of being the actor you are.

What do you think makes Thomas Crown such an enduring character?

When I made my rendition and produced it with my late dear friend Beau St. Clair, I wanted to steal art. I didn’t want to steal diamonds or money. I wanted to steal paintings. It was against all the political correctness of his time and space. Thomas Crown was a man who had everything in life: wealth, fortune, intellect. But he didn’t have love. So it was a love story for me.

When we were looking for the film’s art, I suggested René Magritte: the bowler hats, the red tie, the great coat. Magritte is someone I find spellbinding, captivating, and always has a narrative which is almost cinematic. So that’s where the bowler hats came from. The visible and the invisible: Visible with an apple in front of a face, but you don’t see the face. And I thought that translated well to the enigma of Thomas Crown.

Pierce Brosnan and Callum Turner, The Only Living Boy In New York, 2017.

Having played James Bond yourself, I’m curious how you’re following the conversation around this upcoming chapter.

[Laughs.] Oh, I’m just an audience member now. I’m just the man in the street who is eager to see who is going to play this epic role of cinematic history. All the men who are on the list now are actors I admire. Callum, Callum Turner is someone I’ve worked with, and he’s so strong. They all have a voice and a physique, and a presence on film. They all have longevity as actors, all of these young men.

Pierce Brosnan as 007 in The World Is Not Enough, 1999.

What would you say to the next actor stepping into 007?

Whoever plays the role, I wish him the very best of life and strength and courage. You know, it’s hard to tell who it would be, but I eagerly await to hear the news and the celebration of the next James Bond.

Martin Campbell gave your era such a memorable introduction with GoldenEye. Now, with Denis Villeneuve taking on the franchise, what are you most curious to see him bring to Bond?

I think we are going to be blown away. I really do. [Villeneuve] is such an iconoclastic director. His work is visionary, and his stealth and imagination of camera work and storytelling is so visceral and sensuous. It’s going to be great. It’s going to be truly magnificent. Of course, we all get sentimental and nostalgic, and you have to give it time and be patient, and it’s always such a delightful game. But Villeneuve is someone who I have great admiration for, and I look forward to seeing the work.

Pierce Brosnan as Remington Steele, 1986.

Pierce Brosnan as Remington Steele, 1986.

You’ve played some of cinema’s most impeccably dressed men! Have those characters influenced the way you dress in your own life?

I have always been, I suppose, a clothes horse. When I played Remington Steele, I delved into the work of Cary Grant, another emblem of cinema that I’ve admired. Bob Butler, who directed it, said, “We’re making an old movie,” so I styled myself and had the joy of wearing beautiful suits every week. That continues through my life.

As I’ve gotten older, I used to try to rebel against the look, character, and style of actor I had created for myself. Now I embrace it more because it excites me. I love the elegance of tailored clothes and dressing up, and fitting into the season, the gale of emotion, the world around you.

You’ve got some great hunting coats in MobLand too.

Rebecca Hale, the costume designer, has brought so many great ingredients to the world of Conrad. He’s an Irishman from a hard part of Irish life, the Troubles, a mangled life of abuse and violence. He wants to fit into the world of the Cotswolds and be the gentleman. There’s this magnificent coat in MobLand, where Conrad has a shootout, and they made a magnificent overcoat, which I managed to keep from last season. And, of course, I step back and just revel at what Dame Helen Mirren does. She is such an empress of fashion herself.

When Vanity Fair last caught up with you, around your first solo exhibition, you’d already been painting and curating work for years. How has your relationship with art evolved since then?

I had, yes. I had the exhibition three years ago, and it was a great success in the sense that I had the courage to step out and show the work. I have a body of work now that has progressed, and hopefully I will have another showing here, maybe in London.

Do you find that painting gives you something different from acting, or do the two creative practices feed into each other?

Both are essential to my life. Acting is how I make my living and provide for my family. And to be able to have a lifestyle that is not only creative but productive, and then is hopefully entertaining, because you’re working towards an audience.

The practice of my art is a constant exploration of inner life, inner thoughts, inner emotions expressed through color and form. Having lived in Kauai for 25 years, there’s a wonderful artist there who’s become my teacher, Saim Caglayan. Both are necessary to my life. They soothe me and frustrate me and challenge me and exhilarate me—sometimes all in the same space of day and time.

Yes! I was sketching when I was doing Burberry. There was a lovely landscape down there, and I have my sketchbook with me at all times. I wanted so much to be an artist, to be a writer, a poet, to live a creative life. I have no real head for figures or the abstraction of figures, but I certainly have a great love for art and the power of art on the wall.

With the holidays coming up, and hopefully a little time to slow down, is there anything you’re hoping to make more time for, creatively or personally?

I have a little time left before I go back to London with my wife, Keely. London is home, and my mother of 94 is there, so I’m looking forward to seeing her. In my studio, I have a number of paintings that I’m quite pleased with, and I’d like to finish a couple more. And I’m really excited to jump into season three of MobLand. I have no idea where the story is going. Conrad is slowly, slowly going bonkers. But the thing is, he’s aware of it, and the love story of Maeve and Conrad lives on. It’s very exciting.

#3612. Perez Hilton's Family Shares 'Positive News' 3 Months After Self-Harm Stream

Perez Hilton’s team and family are offering an encouraging update on the blogger’s recovery three months after his disturbing self-harm livestream.

“It’s been three months since our family began navigating this difficult time,” read a message on Hilton’s website on Tuesday, November 3. “While it hasn’t been easy, we’re grateful to have some positive news to share about Perez’s recovery.”

Hilton, 48, was hospitalized on August 4 following a disturbing TikTok livestream where he appeared to engage in self-harm acts. At the time, the Miami-Dade police confirmed to Us that authorities responded to calls “regarding an individual who was live-streaming acts of self-harm on social media.” Officers were dispatched to Hilton’s home for what they suspected was a “possible suicide” attempt.

Hilton underwent surgery due to significant blood loss. He remained in the hospital before moving to an inpatient facility. In October, Hilton began the next phase of his treatment, a partial hospitalization program (PHP), while residing in supportive housing. He will continue to receive mental health care and support, according to the new message.

“He’s also been able to spend time with his family during approved visits, including a special evening celebrating his mom’s 73rd birthday together with the children,” Tuesday’s statement read, referring to his three kids. “These moments together have meant so much to everyone.”

The message continued, “This entire experience has been a learning process for our family. Like many people who have never been through something like this, we didn’t fully understand just how much time, care, and support recovery from a serious mental health crisis can require. Through conversations with others who have been through similar situations, we’ve come to understand that getting through the initial crisis is only the beginning. There’s no one-size-fits-all timeline, and we’re learning the importance of taking things one step at a time.”

While Hilton’s team and family are unsure of an exact date of when he would be returning home, the statement noted that they are “hopeful that day is getting closer.”

“Most importantly, we want him to have the time and support he needs to continue making progress,” the message read. “In the meantime, the children are doing well, staying busy with school, their activities, and everyday life. They also had a wonderful Halloween! After everything they’ve been through, seeing them smiling, having fun, and simply enjoying being kids has been especially meaningful.”

The statement concluded, “As always, thank you to everyone who has continued to check in and send kind messages. We’re incredibly grateful for your love, compassion, and support. It means so much to our family.”
