#3611. WoW: Forever Is Giving Players A Big Damage Boost For Launch

World of Warcraft: Forever is changing in some major ways for launch, with Blizzard revealing classes across the board will deal more damage as it pursues design solutions that better fit in with Forever's combat.

In a lengthy developer note attached to Forever's launch patch notes, Blizzard outlined its philosophy for its latest version of WoW. It said during the game's nearly month-long beta that it was trying to keep player power in check. That meant every time it gave a class new tools and abilities, it had to tone down others to compensate. Blizzard now thinks that was the wrong approach.

"Those reductions left some iconic abilities feeling lackluster, and closed the door to other potentially exciting design options," Blizzard said. "So over the last two weeks, we've raised damage on classes across the game, and have increased the health of higher-level creatures to compensate."

In addition to classes simply doing more damage, classes themselves are changing in major ways. Elemental Shamans, for example, have had Lava Burst, a key part of their class during the beta, removed entirely. It's an example of what Blizzard said was the developer hastily "turning to Burning Crusade or Wrath-era solutions" rather than creating new ideas for how classes should play in Forever compared to previous versions of WoW.

"Our aim in class design is not perfect numerical equality, but rather for every class to feel valuable to groups they join, with powerful, unforgettable moments brought on by mastering them," Blizzard said. "In Forever this is accomplished by doubling down on the strengths and differences that make each class unique, rather than overly unifying them."

Alongside Shaman, a number of other classes have received significant changes going into launch, particularly Paladin and Rogue, with much of their talent trees almost completely reworked. Every class has received some balance changes.

Though the patch notes are largely dedicated to class changes, there are some other adjustments coming for launch as well. There are a number of tweaks to the game's controller support and bug fixes for various quests. Blizzard stated it additionally increased enemy respawn rates in the world for launch, particularly in lower-level zones. Its goal isn't to completely remove contention for spawns but to make it so players aren't hitting hard bottlenecks.

"Once the initial launch surge of low-level characters has settled down, we will adjust the lower-level zones down to more typical rates," Blizzard said. 

You can find the full WoW: Forever launch patch notes below. WoW: Forever launches November 4. Ahead of launch, read up on the best WoW: Forever addons to install so you're ready on day one. In other news, Blizzard revealed its plans for how often players should expect Forever updates, as well how it's looking to avoid dead servers in the future.

WoW: Forever November 2 Launch Patch Notes

Bug Fixes

  • Throw will now correctly use the 0.5 second windup timer (was incorrectly using the throwing weapon’s attack speed).
  • Legacy Reward - Replica Ironforge Air Rifle can now correctly be used on allies that also have one equipped.
    • Duration of the quitter debuff reduced to 40 seconds (was 5 minutes).
    • Duration of the stun reduced to 2.5 seconds (was 3 seconds).
  • All Races now have the correct amount of base stats. For example, Tauren Warriors now start with the correct +5 strength relative to Human Warriors (was incorrectly +2). This fix was also applied to High Order and Windshaper Skyborne base stats.
  • Roots that occur from Procs now correctly have Diminishing Returns. Includes Frostbite, Entrapment, Improved Wing Clip, Counterattack, and Improved Hamstring.

Classes

  • Developer’s notes: Over the course of Beta, we came to the realization that trying to hold ourselves roughly to Classic power budgets for each class meant that every new element we added needed to come at the expense of something else. Those reductions left some iconic abilities feeling lackluster, and closed the door to other potentially exciting design options. So over the last two weeks, we’ve raised damage on classes across the game, and have increased the health of higher level creatures to compensate. This additional “headroom” has allowed us to tune things to a place that we hope feels better overall. Beyond that, some of this round of changes reflects areas where we were likely hasty in turning to Burning Crusade- or Wrath-era solutions rather than carving out new ones that better fit into the Forever combat model. Our aim in class design is not perfect numerical equality, but rather for every class to feel valuable to the groups they join, with powerful, unforgettable moments brought on by mastering them. In Forever this is accomplished by doubling down on the strengths and differences that make each class unique, rather than overly unifying them.
  • Developers’ notes: We’ve used the data and feedback gathered during Beta testing to get everything tuned to a reasonable place. However, the only true test of that tuning is the game itself. With the exception of bugs and serious outliers, we don’t plan on making big tuning changes between now and the opening of the raids next month. Once we have sufficient data from players leveling past 30 and engaging in a wide range of content, we expect that we will do a large tuning pass based on our data. And this is all merely a starting point for the classes in Forever, which will continue to evolve over the course of the months and years ahead just as they did following the original launch in 2004.
  • Various talents no longer have a penalty to their chance to trigger when casting spells of a low rank.
    • This penalty does still apply to Blizzard. Blizzard continues to have a reduced chance to trigger Arcane Concentration, Frostbite, and Fingers of Frost when casting a rank learned more than 12 levels lower than the caster’s current level.
  • Learning new spells will no longer cause them to be automatically added to your action bars.
  • Training costs on have been adjusted for all classes.
    • Most abilities learned at the same level have the same cost to train, with the exception of Priest race-specific abilities.
    • Total cost to train class abilities from 1-60 is now between 206 and 207 gold for all classes.
    • Warlocks costs are reduced by the expected costs of buying Grimoires for their pets.

If either spell expires due to being dispelled, the target is healed for 50% of your Spirit instead.”

      • Flurry changed to a 3-point granting 10/20/30% increased attack speed for 3 swings after a critical strike (was 5 points granting 5/10/15/20/25% increased attack speed).
      • New Talent: Improved Whirlwind. Row 6. 2 Point. Passive. Reduces the cooldown of your Whirlwind ability by 1/2 seconds and increases the damage it deals to the closest enemy by 15/30%.
      • Bloodthirst now has Death Wish as a required talent.
    • Protection
      • Defiance: Threat bonus increased to 7/13/20% from 5/10/15%.

Player versus Player

  • In the Darkspear Islands battleground, dropping the flag no longer places the “Recently Dropped Flag” debuff on the player who dropped it.

Races

  • Dwarf
    • Earth Fury (2% increased critical strike damage and healing) removed.
    • Added: Artisan’s Precision - Increases hit chance with spells and attacks by 1%.
  • Human
    • Ruthless now increases critical chance by 1% (was 2%).
    • Human Spirit now increases Spirit by 10% (was 5%).
  • Orc
    • Savage removed (1% increased critical strike chance).
    • Command re-added, increasing Warlock and Hunter pet damage by 5%.
    • Blood Fury’s cooldown reduced to 2 minutes (was 3 minutes).
  • Skyborne
    • Wind-Blessed Haste bonus reduced to 2% (was 3%).
    • Read Leyline now increases Mana and Health regeneration by 50% (was 100%), with a 15-second duration. This ability cannot be used while Innervate is active, and will be replaced by Innervate as a more powerful effect.
    • Using Read Leyline at a Ley Line now also grants “Attuned” for 1 hour. While Attuned, the benefit of Read Leyline is increased to 100% regeneration increase. Attuned persists through death, and is removed upon entering a raid.
    • Skysight is now a 15% increased movement speed (was 10%), with a 15-second duration.
    • Using Skysight at an elemental convergence now also grants “Charged” for 1 hour. While Charged, the benefit of Skysight is a 30% movement speed increase. Charged persists through death, and is removed upon entering a raid.
  • Tauren
    • Plainsrunning now grants 2% movement speed per stack (was 1%), for a total max increase of 60% (was 30%).
    • Plainsrunning no longer increases mounted movement speed.
    • Endurance no longer provides any modifiers beyond 5% increased Health (no hit chance or critical damage modifiers).
  • Troll
    • Berserking duration increased to 15 seconds (was 10 seconds).
  • Undead
    • Cannibalize can once again be used while immune to Physical damage.
    • Fixed an issue where Touch of the Grave was not activating frequently enough.
    • Fixed an issue where Touch of the Grave was leaving a beam visual behind.
    • Touch of the Grave internal cooldown reduced to 15 seconds (was 25 seconds).

Gamepad Support

  • Gamepad Support has entered a complete functional state.
    • In World of Warcraft: Forever, all major gameplay and core user interface experiences can be played with a controller, including movement, spells, interactions, UI navigation, etc.
    • Gamepad settings can be customized through Edit Mode and the Options menu.
  • Action Bars
    • AoE items bound to the Gamepad Action Bar can now be used and placed at a targeted location.
      • Press the Action Bar button again to confirm placement, consistent with ground-targeted AoE spells.
    • Fixed an issue where changing the current keyboard and mouse Action Bar page would cause Gamepad Action Bar buttons to be offset.
    • Fixed an issue where Gamepad Action Bar settings were not immediately reflected while in Edit Mode.
  • Add-ons
    • Improved Gamepad UI compatibility with user-created add-ons to reduce the likelihood of add-on conflicts causing interface issues.
  • Bags and Inventory
    • Fixed an issue where Gamepad focus could move away from the inventory after confirming or canceling the destruction of an item.
    • Fixed an issue where horizontal Gamepad navigation could behave incorrectly when moving between bag columns of different heights.
    • Fixed an issue where navigating the inventory with a Gamepad during a trade could cause a Lua error.
    • Fixed an issue where opening individual bags with the keyboard and mouse UI could cause a Lua error after switching from the Gamepad UI.
    • Improved bag management when using a Gamepad.
    • Improved the Gamepad Bag UI.
      • Added updated visuals and clearer bag states.
      • Added remaining bag space and ammo count indicators.
      • Improved bag prompts and interactions.
      • Improved Keyring navigation and highlighting.
      • Improved the inventory search layout.
  • Character Select & Ruleset Selection
    • Added Gamepad support for navigating and interacting with ruleset selection screens.
    • Fixed an issue where newly created characters were not automatically selected when returning to the Character Select screen while using a Gamepad.
  • Cinematics
    • Added Gamepad support for skipping or exiting cinematics.
  • Combat and Targeting
    • Added Gamepad support for targeting a previously assigned Focus Target.
      • LB + RB + Face Down can be used to select your Focus Target.
      • The target context menu displays Clear Focus when your current target is also your Focus Target.
    • Friendly corpses can now be targeted with a Gamepad.
      • Friendly Analog Targeting can target friendly corpses.
      • Friendly Tab Targeting can target friendly corpses.
    • Improved Gamepad targeting for critters.
      • Hostile Analog Targeting can target critters.
      • Soft Targeting can target critters.
    • Improved Gamepad targeting of enemy players.
      • Enemy players can no longer be selected by Friendly Analog Targeting.
      • Enemy players can be selected by Hostile Analog Targeting regardless of PvP flag status.
    • Units behind the player can now be selected with Analog Targeting when they remain visible on screen.
    • Feign Death units that remain attackable can now be targeted if and only if the Gamepad reticle is positioned over them.
    • Fixed an issue where certain attackable enemies could incorrectly display an Interact icon when using a Gamepad.
    • Fixed an issue where looting or closing the loot window could leave a corpse incorrectly locked as the player’s target.
  • Flight Paths
    • Added Gamepad support for ending a flight path early using the Back/Cancel action.
      • Players will dismount at the next available flight point.
  • Navigation and Focus
    • Fixed an issue where Gamepad focus could be lost from the Options panel after closing a graphics settings confirmation dialog.
    • Updated popup behavior so non-user-initiated popups no longer automatically steal Gamepad focus.
      • These popups can be explicitly focused using the View/Select action or equivalent controller input.
    • Updated Gamepad navigation prompts to use LT and RT button indicators when navigating between supported UI panels.
  • Pets
    • Added Gamepad support for the Pet Move command.
      • Pet placement can be confirmed using the Interact button or by activating the ability again.
  • Professions
    • Fixed an issue where Gamepad users could not use the Train action at Profession Trainers when a skill upgrade was the only available option.
    • Fixed an issue where the Gamepad prompt for removing a Profession did not indicate that the button needed to be held.
  • Quests
    • Fixed an issue where viewing quest details in a different map region with a Gamepad could cause a Lua error.
  • Swing Timers
    • Fixed an issue where the Off-Hand Swing Timer could fail to appear after logging in on dual-wielding characters.
  • Tooltips and UI
    • Added Gamepad support for adjusting opacity in the Color Picker.
    • Fixed an issue where Gamepad LB and RB prompts could incorrectly appear in the Equipment Manager while using the keyboard and mouse UI.
    • Updated Gamepad tooltips to remain visible rather than allowing them to be toggled on or off with the controller.

Items

  • Bags
    • Bags will no longer automatically equip into available bag slots and must now be manually equipped by the player.

Quests and World

  • Adjusted respawn rates for many different areas in the world.
    • Developers’ notes: Our goal with these adjustments is to properly support large player volumes at launch, so that players aren’t hitting hard bottlenecks and can continue to enjoy the game. Some contention for spawns is expected and part of the experience - it is not our goal to remove that. These adjusted rates are generally on the faster side in lower-level zones - with starting zones being the fastest - and gradually fall to slower rates as you level up, consistent with when players naturally spread out across the many zones available in WoW Forever. Once the initial launch surge of low-level characters has settled down, we will adjust the lower-level zones down to more typical rates.
  • Adjusted experience values on various quests.
  • Adjusted pre-requisites and level settings on some quests to improve flow across the world.
  • Added mouseover tooltips for objectives on various quests.
  • Added missing point-of-interest markers and adjusted incorrect ones on various quests.
  • Fixed incorrect zone sorts in the quest log on various quests.
  • Fixed various quests where destroying the associated item would not abandon the quest, and vice versa.
  • Fixed an issue where some satyr were classified as humanoids instead of demons. They are now 100% more scared of Paladins.
  • Alterac Mountains
    • Fixed an issue where Dalaran Summoners were really amazingly good at summoning and would summon until their little hearts couldn’t summon anymore. And then they’d summon some more anyway.
  • Barrens
    • You can now speak to Rethgar Deathgate to begin the event for “Counterattack!” if it is not currently active.
    • The Alliance Outrunners now spawn in random locations.
  • Darkshore
    • The quest “Holy Diver” now gives an XP reward.
  • Mulgore
    • Gloomrise Hatchlings now give lower XP, commensurate with their lower health values.
  • Orgrimmar
    • Fixed an issue during “Hidden Enemies” where the Lieutenant’s Insignia would remain in inventory after quest completion.
  • Ruins of Lordaeron
    • Ruins of Lordaeron dungeon quests now consistently require a minimum of level 15 to start (was a mix of 15 and 16), and some pre-requisites have been adjusted.
  • Teldrassil
    • The Cleft - There are now slightly fewer spiders in this area for the quest “Twisted Hatred”.
  • Wetlands
    • Fixed an issue where Carnage reset near the end of the fight for the quest “Carnage”.
    • Fixed an issue during “Destruction in Deadmines” where Alba Fairmoon would become unavailable to turn-in the quest.

#3610. 10 Shows Like 'A Different World' You Should Watch Next

Ross Johnson writes about television, film, and literature for Lifehacker. He has a degree in political science from the University of Rochester and has previously been a legal writer and editor for Thomson Reuters, for which he later traveled around India and the Middle East as an educator specializing in American English style and grammar for adults.

Ross has been an actor on stage, in commercials, and in independent films since childhood, and has written hundreds of articles and essays on genre literature and cinema for Barnes & Noble, Gizmodo, Kotaku, and Yahoo! Entertainment.Ross produces the Swan Songs film podcast and hosts The Sound of Tomorrow, a pop culture and current affairs radio show based in Rochester, New York, where he lives with his husband and dogs and supports the local arts and cinema scene. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

The original A Different World was a groundbreaking sitcom in its era, spending six seasons highlighting Black academic drive among a cast of characters so indelible that we're now checking in on them decades later. Spearheaded by Queen Sugar's Felicia Pride, the update has been a critical and ratings hit for Netflix, earning the rarest prize of all in streaming television: a quick second season renewal. While you're waiting for season two, here are some other smart coming-of-age shows that blend heart and humor with realistic drama.

An easy pairing with A Different World, this show follows Black-ish's Zoey Johnson (Yara Shahidi) as she leaves home to attend a (fictional) California liberal arts college (the last couple of post-graduation seasons shift the focus to her brother Andre, played by Marcus Scribner). The emphasis is on driven young people who are capable of making big mistakes on the path to adulthood. A true comedy-drama, Grown-ish feels real(-ish) in a way that few other college shows have managed. Stream Grown-ish on Hulu.

Adapted from and expanding upon the 2014 movie, this show takes us to a (fictional) Ivy League school for a comedy-drama that tackles campus life and politics from a rather different perspective than that of Rooster. Logan Browning leads the ensemble cast as Sam White, who kind of inadvertently starts the titular radio show following a racially charged incident on campus. Far from the racial screed that some bad-faith YouTubers seem to find it, it's never shy about confronting the complicated and occasionally silly contradictions of campus activism, with each episode approaching life at Winchester University from a different character's perspective. Stream Dear White People on Netflix.

Kimberly (Pauline Chalamet) is an endlessly naïve scholarship student; Bela (Amrit Kaur) is an aspiring comedy writer on the make for the hottest guys; Whitney (Alyah Chanelle Scott) is an overachieving athlete and senator’s daughter; and Leighton (Reneé Rapp) is a closeted sorority girl. They're all randomly assigned to room together as freshmen at the fictional Essex College in Vermont. Created by Mindy Kaling and Justin Noble, this comedy-drama isn't nearly as salacious as its title suggests. There's sex for sure, but mostly it's a funny, queer-friendly show that's a little less about one overarching romance than it is about growing up, and the value of female friendship. Stream The Sex Lives of College Girls on HBO Max.

Even though we're backing up a couple of years to follow teens in their high school years, this British import's setting is a decent match, finding its students living away from home and family for the first time in their lives. At the fictional prestigious boarding school St. Gilbert’s, five Black teens are newly attending on scholarships, but their integration into the existing cliques is less than smooth—especially given that they're there largely as a PR stunt. Boarders blends teen romance, coming-of-age drama, and a delightful willingness to take the piss when it comes to the whole "rich private school" thing. Stream Boarders on Tubi.

Another modern take on a beloved '80s/'90s sitcom, this one's a bit different, serving as a total reimagining with no narrative connection to the original. And while A Different World is a comedy with dramatic heft, this one's more of a straight drama. It’s jarring for fans of the beloved original to tune in to find a serious show with the same premise as the Will Smith original—one that often leans into heavy realism. Jabari Banks plays, er, Will Smith, a 16-year-old from West Philadelphia who moves in with his auntie and uncle in Bel-Air following a gun charge and a run-in with a Philly drug lord. Banks is charismatic and believable, bringing a ton of personality to a show that occasionally veers down dark alleys. Stream Bel-Air on Peacock.

Comedian Benito Skinner plays himself, kinda, in this buzzy comedy that sees a former high school jock facing his freshman year in college while desperately trying to convince himself and everyone else that he's as straight as they come (relatable, except for the jock part). Much of the appeal is in its deft blending of tones: It's both a frequently raunchy college comedy and a sweet coming-of-age story about accepting yourself without worrying about what everyone else thinks. The cast includes Adam DiMarco (The White Lotus) and Rish Shah (Ms. Marvel), and, though it's more a story of one young man's coming of age, there's a strong ensemble backing him up. Stream Overcompensating on Prime Video.

The heart of All American (for most of its run) is Spencer James (Daniel Ezra), based on real-life NFL linebacker Spencer Paysinger. A star player for his high school team in Crenshaw, he's recruited by the coach (Taye Diggs) of a team in Beverly Hills to come and play for them, forcing Spencer to navigate two very different worlds while trying to build a life and potential career. Stream All American on Netflix.

Following a family tragedy, the already awkward 15-year-old Devi Vishwakumar (Maitreyi Ramakrishnan) has a pretty terrible freshman year of high school, and decides that she’s going to turn things around the following year, hoping that a nearly academic study of sex will get her the boyfriend(s) her raging hormones have begun to demand. It works, to a point—but getting a surprise yes to sex from her crush leads her to question what she’s really ready for. More about burgeoning sexuality than sex specifically, this Mindy Kaling-produced series is both honest and charming. Stream Never Have I Ever on Netflix.

For realism in a show about the college experience, you could do a lot worse than this docuseries following several students at Gallaudet University, a school for deaf and hard-of-hearing young adults. In one sense, it's a specific setting where perspectives on deafness vary wildly, even in Gallaudet's self-contained world (aside from being a show about academically driven and horny college students, this is also a great primer for hearing people about some of the issues). But even for all of that, the challenges in building a life and future away from home are pretty universally relatable. Stream Deaf U on Netflix.

There's a reason A Different World has returned in 2026, and a lot of that has to do with the fact that there was nothing else on TV quite like it back in the late '80s and early '90s. For all of its sitcom sensibilities, the show tried hard (especially after multi-hyphenate creator Debbie Allen arrived to rework things after its first season) to paint a realistic picture of college life and an HBCU. Of the few shows on TV with largely Black casts, almost none would go so far as to highlight achievement and excellence; A Different World managed to do so while building a cast of characters so memorable that we're more than willing to catch up with them nearly forty years later. Stream A Different World on Netflix.

#3609. Bill Hader Also Played The Cat In The Hat On SNL, And It Was Not A Good Experience

This weekend Bill Hader is the voice of the animated The Cat In The Hat movie on the 2026 release schedule. But did you know that over a decade ago he totally dressed up as the beloved Dr. Seuss character for a Saturday Night Live sketch? When we chatted with the SNL alum, I had to ask about the memories of playing the role IRL.

Of course, Mike Myers famously took the live-action approach for the 2003 book-to-screen adaptation. In our interview, Hader seems to counts himself lucky to have just lent the voice to the character after spending a day in the literal paws of the character way back when. In his words:

I’m very happy to do it animated because that suit was very hot. And the makeup took a long time. It was the second music number, and then another pre-tape thing that I wasn't in just so they could put all the makeup on me. It was the last sketch of the night, so we did it really fast. So yeah, it was really hot and I had all that stuff on my face. I don't know how Mike Myers did it.

Myers' own process took two and a half hours and was very hot to act in a yak-hair suit all day. Jim Carrey had it even worse as The Grinch. He had to go through such a grueling process a specialist in torture was hired to help him withstand the eight-hour get ready time. In our interview above, you can see Quinta Brunson school Hader on what happened and watch his real-time reaction.

Instead of going through all that makeup time for months, it was just for one night. He played the character on October 11, 2014 in an episode he hosted in the season right after his exit from the show following an eight-year run. You can check out the sketch below:

It’s such a funny spin on the classic children’s book. When two sibling children are bored on a rainy day, they conjure up The Cat in the Hat, but something unexpected happens: he’s already acquainted with their mom, Linda. Playtime with the whimsical figure turns into an awkward reunion between The Cat and Linda. The best line has to be when Linda says: “He’s reliable. I don’t have to say a rhyme to make him come home.” ‘

And then, Linda’s husband ends up being Thing 2, who goes by Jona-Thing now. He comes home disappointed to see The Cat In The Hat with his wife and kids. The sketch hilariously ends with The Cat In The Hat saying “But oh, the places she let me go!” as he leaves them, which is obviously a NSFW reference to another Dr. Seuss book.

When CinemaBlend also spoke to the movie’s writer/directors Erica Rivinoja and Alessandro Carloni, we had to ask if the SNL sketch was involved at all with casting Hader. Here’s what Rivinoja told us:

It was completely random, of course, but we might wanna do a sequel with that character and with Linda. We're very excited about Linda.

Hader’s animated version of The Cat in the Hat is much different than SNL because it isn’t a parody like his first run as the character was. It’s a more family-friendly retelling of the picture book with an expanded story about where The Cat comes from, and involves an imaginative plot line that’s perfect for the medium of animation. It hits theaters this Friday, November 6.

Now she's into covering YA television and movies, and plenty of horror. Word webslinger. All her writing should be read in Sarah Connor’s Terminator 2 voice over.

#3608. GTA 6 Is Getting A Physical Map–Here’s How To Get One For Free Or Very Cheap

Rockstar Games has confirmed more details about Grand Theft Auto 6's impending release on November 19, including more information about physical goodies. While the game itself won't be available on a disc, Rockstar is offering a printable physical GTA 6 cover art poster and a map of the game's setting, Leonida.

The poster and Leonida map will be available for free as digital downloads on GTA 6's official website on November 19. A double-sized physical version of the poster will be available "shortly after launch" from the Rockstar Store for 99 cents. Alternatively, it's free with any purchase from the Rockstar Store.

Back in the day, Rockstar used to include fold-out posters in the box for GTA games featuring the game's cover art and map. But GTA 6 is a digital-only game. Players can buy a physical GTA 6 box at retail stores, but it won't include a disc, only a code for a digital download. Rockstar hasn't said if it will include anything extra in the box.

Some retailers are apparently trying to sweeten the deal to encourage people to buy from them. It was recently reported that Walmart orders of GTA 6 will include some kind of "surprise." When the Switch 2 released, some Walmart orders for the console included "game-ready" snacks like soda and chips.

In other news, Rockstar just recently announced when GTA 6 preloading begins and when the game unlocks--players in the US will be among the last people in the world to get in.

#3607. What Happened to Christina Downer? BF Arrested in 'SNL' Writer's Sister's Death

More than a year after Saturday Night Live writer Jimmy Fowlie’s sister, Christina Downer, vanished, her former boyfriend has been charged with her murder.

The Los Angeles County District Attorney’s Office announced on November 2, 2026, that Delorean Bijon Brandon has been charged with one count of murder and two felony counts of injuring a spouse. A codefendant, Kaylee Markowski, was hit with one felony charge of accessory after the fact.

“More than a year has passed since Christina Downer vanished and her family and friends have dealt with uncertainty amid the profound loss of someone they loved so much,” District Attorney Nathan J. Hochman said in a statement. “Although Ms. Downer has not been located, we are charging two individuals today who are accused of playing a role in her death and disappearance and we will hold them accountable for their actions.”

Authorities believe that Brandon killed Downer on or around September 19, 2025, and that Markowski, 34, allegedly helped dispose of her body. The DA’s office confirmed that Downer and Brandon were in a relationship at the time of her disappearance.

Brandon has also been charged with assaulting his wife on two separate occasions in 2022, prosecutors said.

The LAPD offered additional insight in a press release on Friday, October 30, explaining that Downer’s ex-husband requested a welfare check in December 2025 after he was unable to reach her for “an extended period of time.” Brandon allegedly told police that Downer had moved out months earlier and claimed she left behind all her belongings, including her vehicle and her dog.

Downer’s cell phone was later discovered “washed ashore at Santa Monica Beach,” and detectives from the LAPD’s Robbery-Homicide Division took over the investigation.

It’s not currently clear whether Brandon or Markowski have entered pleas. The investigation remains ongoing.

In the months before her disappearance, Downer and her boyfriend were both tangled in court filings involving his ex-girlfriend. Court documents obtained by Us confirmed that Downer asked Los Angeles Superior Court for a temporary civil harassment restraining order in September 2024. (There is no suggestion that the 2024 or 2025 restraining order requests have any connection to Downer’s disappearance.)

In the filing, Downer accused the ex of harassing the couple from Christmas Day 2023 to March 2024 and again from July 2024 through September 2024.

“[She] threatened to beat me up, stole my spare key and copied it. Threatens to break into my home. Stole his zip drive and has been blackmailing me with the videos on the zip drive. Actually sent a topless video of me in my home to people I don’t know while attacking my reputation. Put AirTags on [my] boyfriend’s car. Calls from blocked numbers. Threatens to keep releasing personal videos from this stolen zip drive,” Downer wrote.

Downer argued that the alleged harassment “has done irreparable damage” from a mental health standpoint because it was “nonstop on a daily basis.”

“[There are] endless messages to me, my boyfriend or others attacking my character,” she wrote in her TRO petition.

Downer also asked for protection for her orange tabby cat, Pumpkin, who she said was in the ex’s possession at the time. “This is my cat with my boyfriend,” she clarified. “I found this cat and we decided during our first split that the cat would stay with him because I was traveling. He moved in with her and moved out a month ago, and she won’t give the cat back. I fear for his safety.”

The case was dismissed in October 2024 after Downer failed to attend a court hearing, and court documents had not been served to the ex.

Brandon filed domestic violence restraining orders against the same ex-girlfriend in July and September 2025 — just three months before Fowlie first went public about his missing sister. He claimed his ex threatened to shoot him, slashed his tire and sent harassing emails. Downer was named in the documents as someone who witnessed what happened.

He claimed in June 2025 that his ex “mentioned that if I returned to her property uninvited that she would shoot me in the head” and said she owned a BB gun.

“We were on and off in [a] relationship and every time I wanted to move on then she would get aggressive,” he wrote. “She was upset that I wanted to finally take [the] last of my belongings from her place because I was no longer living there and moved on with my life with Christina.”

In the 2025 filings, he referred to Downer as his significant other and someone he wanted protected under the TRO. “She writes us harassing emails all the time. And harassing job sites to get Christina not hired,” he wrote.

Both TRO requests were dismissed in August and September 2025 because Brandon did not appear in court and his ex had not been served.

When reached for comment, Brandon told Us: “I didn’t want to file those restraining orders at all against my [ex]. She (Christina) made me do it because she said that if I ever left her again then this (restraining order) would keep me away from my [ex].”

He added of Downer’s disappearance, “I’m just as worried about her disappearance, just as much as everyone else. I don’t have anything else to say about her, just that I miss her wherever she may be.”

Fowlie, who famously wrote SNL’s viral “Domingo” sketch, initially asked for the public’s help in December 2025.

“My sister has been missing and we are worried that she isn’t safe,” he wrote via Instagram. “Her married name is Downer but she may go by Christina Fowlie. Please share this so that if anyone has seen her, they can give any information to the police.”

SNL cast members Sarah Sherman and Chloe Fineman, Amy Schumer, Ariana Madix, Scheana Shay and Casey Wilson all offered Fowlie support in the wake of his sister’s disappearance.

On Christmas Eve 2025, Fowlie amplified the case again, revealing he had last spoken to Downer nearly a month earlier. “Christina is very attached to her dog Rex. He’s a min pin and if you see her chances are he’d be with her. Last seen in Koreatown. I heard from her on Nov 26th. She was active on social media up to Dec 15th.”

In April 2026, Fowlie shared a devastating update. “The LAPD has informed our family that Christina is no longer alive, and the case has officially transitioned from a missing person to a homicide investigation,” he wrote. “Our prayers for her to be found safely have transformed into prayers for the truth to be revealed and for those responsible to be held accountable.”

Fowlie added that he believed Downer’s phone and social media were “compromised” in the weeks before she disappeared. “The individual(s) in possession of her phone used it to hide the fact she was gone, to ask for money and to create a false narrative that she was going ‘off the grid,’” he wrote. “I am sharing this because I believe that whoever is responsible is hoping to erase her in every way possible.”

#3606. Google Quietly Linked Your Phone Number Across Your Accounts, but You Can Stop It

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

In recent weeks, Google has been automatically connecting Android users' phone numbers to every Google account they are signed into on their devices—without requesting consent to do so. This means that if you are logged into personal, work, and disposable accounts on your Android phone, Google may have silently verified and linked your number with all of them even if you've deliberately kept them separate. If you that's not something you want, there's a way to fix it.

As Android Authority reports, some Android users have recently received confirmation emails from an official Google address stating that their phone number has been verified. Google has required occasional phone number re-verification but appears to have updated its support documentation about a year ago to make this feature opt-out by default. As part of this process, Google also adds your phone number to all Google Accounts that are signed in on the device, including current accounts and phone numbers and any that are added or updated in the future.

Updating this setting does not disconnect phone numbers and Google accounts that have already been linked. You can find out which are which via your Google Account Personal Info page. Select your profile picture in the upper-right corner to go through each signed-in account and open the Phone section to select and delete any numbers you don't want associated.

Finally, Malwarebytes advises scrolling down to the Usage section on the Phone page to view which services are listed as well as reviewing your Security & sign-in settings. If you added your phone number for two-step verification or to a separate app like Google Pay, deleting it from the Phone page won't remove it entirely from your account, and you'll need to update those settings separately. Automatic phone verification shouldn't be the culprit here, but it's useful to audit what your number is being used for and on which accounts if you want to keep things separate.

#3605. Parties That Changed the World: Barbie’s Premiere and Gone With the Wind’s Debut

The world’s most famous doll was inspired by a spunky, high-end call girl named Lilli. Described as a “gold digger, exhibitionist, and floozy,” the character of Bild Lilli was created in 1952 by German cartoonist Reinhard Beuthien after he was asked to draw a filler cartoon for the inaugural issue of the tabloid Bild-Zeitung. Lilli, a buxom blonde with a perky ponytail and sky-high stilettos, sat beside a fortune teller. “Can’t you give me the name and address of this tall, handsome, rich man?” she cooed. The cartoon was an instant hit, and in 1955, Lilli was immortalized in plastic.

A year later, Ruth Handler discovered the Lilli doll while on a vacation in Europe. She bought several. One was for her teenage daughter, Barbara, to keep; the rest were brought back to Mattel, the toy company she had cofounded with her husband, Elliot, and businessman Harold Matson. (Mattel is a portmanteau of both men’s names.) Lilli—with comically large breasts, chic outfits, and heavy makeup—was precisely what Handler had been looking for.

Robin Gerber, author of Barbie and Ruth, wrote: “The doll looked too much like a prostitute for the company’s taste,” so Mattel’s design team (slightly) softened Lilli’s exaggerated proportions, renamed her Barbie, after Barbara, and before long, she would become the physical ideal for generations of young girls and women everywhere.

Sixty-four years after Barbie hit shelves, she finally got her close-up in Barbie, a feminist manifesto in a pair of pink stilettos. The film’s premiere and after-party at the Shrine Auditorium marked Warner Bros.’ largest premiere to date—and the cherry on top of a bubble-gum-flavored, years-long marketing blitz. According to Event Marketer, “the affair was like Barbie herself: high-energy, glamorous and very, very, colorful.”

It was a beautiful day in Hollywood. Even by Los Angeles standards, the weather on Sunday, July 9, 2023, was almost impossibly perfect—sunshine, low 70s, and a cool breeze—as if Hollywood itself has been dropped into the fantasy world of Barbie Land.

The event kicked off with a splash. The pink carpet was tricked out with replicas of pieces from the film’s beach scenes: a lifeguard station, a towering lighthouse, faux palm trees, and a 3D ocean wave, with carpeting that shifted colors to mimic sand. A wide range of influencers were invited to get first dibs on photo ops before the stars arrived. But the real showstopper was the two-story replica of Barbie’s Dreamhouse, complete with a 2D faux pool, a DJ spinning tracks, and the trademark spiral slide. “We had to have that slide,” Wendy Robino, SVP of Warner Bros. marketing events, said at the time.

On Sunday, they wore pink: Writer and director Greta Gerwig, along with cast members Issa Rae, America Ferrera, Kate McKinnon, Ryan Gosling, and Michael Cera, turned out for the premiere in every shade of Barbie’s signature color, turning something long dismissed as girly into a celebration of individuality, joy, and girl power.

But the belle of the ball wasn’t one to blend in. After weeks of thinking pink, Margot Robbie—the film’s star and producer—arrived in black. Her custom Schiaparelli look re-created 1960s’ Solo in the Spotlight Barbie: a black sequined dress with a single red rose stitched onto her tulle skirt, matching opera gloves, Manolo Blahnik mules, and a diamond necklace. Movie Star Barbie fully committed to the bit, even clutching a pink handkerchief as she posed in front of a pink Corvette. Robbie’s blond hair was swept into a high ponytail—reminiscent of the one first worn by Lilli.

Following the official screening—marking the first time Barbie was revealed to the public—it was time to party.

The theme was “Barbie’s Blowout Disco Party.” Fittingly, one attraction invited guests inside a glittering, 12-foot pink disco ball. Justin Lefkovitch, whose company Mirrored Media, partnered with Mattel to create it, tells VF the entrance created “a shroud of mystery” for partygoers. Inside, a six-foot 1:1 Dreamhouse showcasing the new Barbie the Movie doll collection was surrounded by gold and silver streamers and over a dozen custom pink disco balls. The goal, Lefkovitch recalls, was to “transport guests into the world of Barbie.”

Nicki Minaj was the first guest to arrive at the party, event producer Austin Johnston tells VF—“five-foot-long hair all the way down to the floor.” A theme park designer by trade, Johnston and his company, AKJohnston, transformed the after-party into what he calls a “pop-up museum.” Barbie Land’s pastel-colored cul-de-sac was re-created as “a 65-foot-tall, 70-foot-wide” inflatable, its landmarks crammed together like a kitschy postcard. At the end of Barbie’s driveway, Mark Ronson presided over a hot pink DJ booth, playing hits from the soundtrack by Ice Spice, Dua Lipa (a.k.a. Mermaid Barbie), and Nicki Minaj—whom Johnston had to “very kindly” ask to get off Barbie’s Corvette.

Tucked beneath the second-floor mezzanine, a series of alcoves became larger-than-life photo sets, with photographers on hand to capture guests in action. Partygoers could retrace Barbie’s journey to the Real World—by bike, boat, and rocket ship—or step inside the Kendom man cave, Weird Barbie’s house, and life-size Barbie and Ken toy boxes. Not everyone hired to re-create Barbie Land had actually seen the movie by then; only a handful were invited to be part of that “really restricted small group,” Johnston says.

At the center of the room, guests sipped pink cocktails under a giant disco ball while an 11-foot, glitter-coated pink B twirled above. Another bar doubled as a fashion show, with four life-size mannequins dolled up for disco in original costumes from the film’s dance number, including Barbie’s gold sequined jumpsuit and the Kens’ matching white-and-gold tracksuits.

Obviously, the food was on theme too. Wolfgang Puck catered the evening’s Barbie-Q, serving grilled salmon, summer melon salad, roasted Pink Fir apple potatoes, char siu glazed grilled chicken, and charred tricolor cauliflower.

Even the night’s corporate sponsors knew better than to steal Barbie’s spotlight. OPI set up a nail salon, and Xbox provided a gaming station where players had their pick of two General Motors rides: Barbie’s Corvette or Ken’s Hummer. A highlight for Johnston was spotting Robbie racing a virtual Hummer while her Australian parents cheered her on. “No one paid her to do that,” he says. “She’s just like, I want to have a drink and play a video game at my premiere.”

For one night in Hollywood, women could be anything. And 84 years earlier, another city had hosted another rager in honor of another larger-than-life heroine. While Los Angeles turned pink for Barbie, Atlanta resurrected the Old South for Scarlett O’Hara.

All hell broke loose when British actor Vivien Leigh was cast as beloved heroine Scarlett O’Hara in the big-screen adaptation of Margaret Mitchell’s epic, Gone With the Wind. Fans and journalists were outraged that such an iconic Southern Belle would be played by a foreigner. At the time, Leigh was yet to star in a Hollywood film and was best known stateside for her affair with Laurence Olivier. Gossip columnist Hedda Hopper sniped: “Out of millions of American women, [producer David O. Selznick] couldn’t find one to suit him.”

Hopper was exaggerating, but not by a lot: During a grueling two-year nationwide search for his leading lady, Selznick reportedly met with over 1,400 actresses. After angry fan letters poured in, Selznick’s publicity machine kicked into overdrive—and eventually, the public came around to the idea that a refined Brit was somehow easier to swallow than a Yankee.

But perhaps the most convincing endorsement came from Leigh’s own leading man. Even Clark Gable, who initially considered Leigh “too demure” for the Southern firecracker, was won over by her dedication and declared she “was Scarlett every minute.” His own casting, meanwhile, had been a dream come true from the thousands who flooded MGM and Selznick’s offices with letters demanding he play Rhett Butler

The shoot was famously plagued by drama, and by the time filming wrapped, the cast and crew had earned themselves a party.

But Selznick had bigger fish to fry—namely, finishing the movie in time for its premiere. He left the party planning to local organizers and his trusted story editor Kay Brown, who had convinced her boss to buy the film rights in the first place. But since Atlanta was still tightly in the grip of Jim Crow, not everyone could join in. Leigh’s costars Hattie McDaniel and Butterfly McQueen were excluded from the festivities.

Selznick argued, unsuccessfully, with local organizers to get McDaniel on the guest list. Gable threatened to not attend the premiere in solidarity with his friend, The Hollywood Reporter stated, but McDaniel ultimately talked him out of it. “While it was unfortunate to exclude Mammy, it was the wisest policy,” Brown wrote, per Matthew Bernstein, former professor of film and media studies at Emory University.

Meanwhile, white Atlanta was gearing up for the party of the century. Former president Jimmy Carter later called it the South’s “biggest event” in his lifetime. According to Time, then governor Eurith D. Rivers was prepared to call in the National Guard, while Mayor Hartsfield urged every woman of Atlanta to dust off her hoop skirts and each man to “sprout a goatee, sideburns, and Kentucky colonel whiskers.”

Hollywood came in hot. Leigh and Gable made their grand entrance by limousine, waving to the 300,000 spectators who lined seven miles of streets in downtown Atlanta—including a number of nonagenarian Confederate veterans who were invited as special guests. Leigh arrived with Olivier while Gable brought his new wife, Carole Lombard. Fun fact: Gable reportedly hadn’t even wanted to play Rhett Butler until Louis B. Mayer offered to help bankroll his divorce so he could marry Lombard.

Of the motorcade, Time wrote: “Crowds larger than the combined armies that fought at Atlanta in July 1864 waved Confederate flags, tossed confetti till it seemed to be snowing, gave three different versions of the Rebel yell, whistled, cheered, goggled.” Leigh wept as the crowd welcomed the British actress “back home,” as if she’d just returned from battle.

The multiday event included a costume ball thrown by the Junior League that would have Abraham Lincoln rolling over in his grave. Decked out in hoop skirts, bustles, and Confederate-era uniforms, 6,000 guests descended on the Municipal Auditorium, which had been transformed into a recreation of the film’s Monster Bazaar. Black participants were relegated to serving or entertaining. Among them was the Ebenezer Baptist Church choir, whose singers reportedly performed dressed as enslaved people in front of a façade of Tara, a fictional plantation from the film. One of the singers was 10-year-old future civil rights hero Martin Luther King Jr.

Vivien Leigh arrived in a velvet gown designed by Walter Plunkett. Though Olivier escorted her costar Olivia de Havilland instead—to keep up appearances—Leigh was the belle of the ball, especially in hometown hero Margaret Mitchell’s absence. Eighteen years earlier, the young novelist had performed a risqué “apache dance” at a charity gala, which cost her her Junior League membership. Now, with Hollywood celebrating her masterpiece, some suspected Mitchell was getting the last laugh by snubbing the biggest party in town.

Young women fangirled all over Gable. According to Time, one woman fainted at the sight of him. Another was given a choice: a Christmas gift or a chance to meet the heartthrob. She chose Gable. After he kissed the 11-year-old, she gasped, “Now am I a woman?”

Governor Rivers declared December 15, 1939, a statewide holiday in honor of Gone With the Wind’s world premiere, the grand finale of the three-day extravaganza. Searchlights swept the Southern sky, and flashbulbs popped as 18,000 spectators crowded Peachtree Street. Even Loew’s Grand Theater got a glow-up. Its Romanesque façade was disguised as a grand Southern plantation—four towering white columns were erected to support a temporary façade with floral garlands, potted trees, and an enormous portrait of Leigh and Gable hung above the entrance.

Inside, all 2,000-plus seats sold out at $10 a pop—the equivalent of about $240 today. That’s not exactly chump change, considering Atlanta was still licking its wounds after the Great Depression. Young women in antebellum costumes greeted guests before Mayor Hartsfield took the stage to kick things off. Selznick and the film’s stars received standing ovations that lasted a full minute. But the loudest cheers were for Mitchell, now in attendance, who joined Leigh and Gable onstage.

The lights dimmed for nearly four hours of melodrama. When Rhett Butler delivered his immortal parting shot—“Frankly, my dear, I don’t give a damn”—the audience reportedly gasped, then erupted in applause as he left Scarlett in his dust.

Before Gone With the Wind—still the highest-grossing film of all time when adjusted for inflation—premieres were usually exclusive screenings in Hollywood or New York. 1939’s antebellum extravaganza turned an entire city into a movie set, setting the stage for modern spectacles like Barbie.

Both parties also offer a revealing snapshot of the societies that threw them. For Gone With the Wind, the industry glorified an imagined past; for Barbie, Hollywood toasted an imagined future. The Barbie premiere wasn’t just a love letter to a feminist film: It was also a giant corporate juggernaut designed to sell a product whose history was tangled up with the very stereotypes the film was questioning. It paid off: Following the film’s theatrical release, Mattel reported a third-quarter increase in worldwide gross billings of 27%, and Barbie toy sales in the United States increased 25% for the July-August combined months compared to the same two-month period a year prior. The immersive premiere, brand collaborations, worldwide activations, and fan participation blurred the line between marketing a movie and creating a cultural event.

The film also became Warner Bros.’ most successful release of all time, grossing $1.4 billion worldwide and making Greta Gerwig the first solo female director admitted into the hallowed halls of the billion-dollar boys club. The premiere celebrated a movie that changed the cultural conversation while handily outgrossing the testosterone-fueled Oppenheimer—a spectacular rebuke to the assumption that chick flicks have a glass ceiling.

Its timing made the celebration particularly potent. In that moment, Hollywood was still finding its footing after the pandemic; the premiere offered something audiences were missing. “It eventized going back to the movies. It eventized the premiere,” says Lefkovitch.

For one night, partygoers got to revel in a fairy tale where women ruled the world. But outside Barbie Land, the irony had all the subtlety of Ken’s Mojo Dojo Casa House. Hollywood was throwing an enormous party celebrating a fantasy of female empowerment while women were still fighting for equality in the real world. There is “definitely some hypocrisy,” agrees Lefkovitch, who made a point of thanking his all-female team.

Decades earlier, Atlanta had thrown its own enormous party, celebrating a fantasy of Southern womanhood while reinforcing the racial and social hierarchies of the real South—and conveniently leaving the horrors of slavery out of the picture. (The film itself did just that, presenting a fictional plantation where the most loyal individuals enjoyed being enslaved.) Black performers were welcome to entertain white audiences, but not to celebrate alongside them; not a single seat inside Loew’s Grand Theater was available to Black moviegoers.

Together, these indignities galvanized the local Black press. In a column for Atlanta Daily World, Reverend John Clarence Wright wrote, “As Atlanta goes mad with the Wind one hundred thousand of her citizens should become more thoughtful than ever of the course that must be pursued to gain their rights as free men and citizens in a land where the spirit of secession and slavery still lives.” With Black moviegoers barred from Southern theaters, the Pittsburgh Courier dryly observed, “Negro reaction… will have to wait until the film comes North.”

The premiere and the film’s success helped propel the NAACP to fight not just individual films, but toward a broader campaign to change Hollywood itself. In 1942, NAACP leader Walter White spoke directly to studio heads in an attempt to persuade them to steer away from demeaning Black stereotypes—like the ones onscreen in Gone With the Wind—and to increase the roles available to Black actors in Hollywood.

White’s approach infuriated the very woman whose absence from the Atlanta premiere had helped expose Hollywood’s hypocrisy: Hattie McDaniel. As a Black woman, McDaniel’s choices were limited—“I’d rather play a maid than be one,” she once said. Writing for Vanity Fair, Hadley Hall Meares noted that McDaniel was “incensed” that White had negotiated with the studios on her behalf, and believed she and her fellow Black actors deserved their own seat at the negotiating table.

McDaniel did get a seat at the 1940 Oscars—but it was at a small table at the edge of the room, separated from her Gone With the Wind costars. The ceremony, after all, was held at the Cocoanut Grove nightclub, which had a strict color line. When her name was called, McDaniel gushed: “I sincerely hope I shall always be a credit to my race and to the motion picture industry.”

Meares described McDaniel’s life as “a tightrope walk.” She was expected to satisfy the white executives who controlled her career, the Black audiences who wanted better representation, and her own ambitions as an actress.

Vivien Leigh also made history that night, becoming the first Brit to win the Oscar for best actress. She dedicated her award to Selznick for his “energy, courage, and very great kindness.” After all, he had been partly responsible for convincing an initially outraged public that Leigh was worthy to play their beloved Scarlett O’Hara. Years later, the Academy lavished Barbie with eight nominations, though it snubbed Gerwig for best director and Robbie for best actress. (Frankly, my dear, they didn’t give a damn about the two women who created Barbie Land.) If Hollywood could build an entire universe in which women ruled the world, why was it still so difficult to imagine one outside the movie theater?

Billie Eilish and Finneas O’Connell took home Barbie’s only Oscar, for best original song. Their winning composition poses Barbie’s existential question while echoing the expectations heaped upon Scarlett, Leigh, McDaniel, Robbie, and Gerwig: “What Was I Made For?”

It turns out the inspiration for Barbie—the quintessential American toy—wasn’t even made for little girls. Lilli dolls were sold to grown men in European tobacco shops and adult toy stores, becoming popular gag gifts. “Men… put them on their car dashboard, dangled them from the rearview mirror, or gave them to girlfriends as a suggestive keepsake,” Gerber wrote. Long before Barbie could be anything, she was something for men.

Eighty-four years apart, Hollywood threw two spectacular parties for women who refused to play by the rules. But the rules were still very much in place when the lights came back up.

#3604. WoW: Forever Won’t Get More Class Balance Changes Any Time Soon

World of Warcraft: Forever is gearing up for launch with some major class balance changes, but don't expect any more for at least a month.

As detailed in Forever's launch patch notes, Blizzard is making some dramatic class changes, including major reworks to Rogue and Paladin talents, in time for release that will result in a big spike in player power. Blizzard said it has used all the data from the game's month-long beta to "get everything tuned to a reasonable place."

However, don't expect additional changes in the near future. Blizzard said it won't be making significant balance changes until sometime next month.

"With the exception of bugs and serious outliers, we don't plan on making big tuning changes between now and the opening of the raids next month," Blizzard wrote in its patch notes. "Once we have sufficient data from players leveling past 30 and engaging in a wide range of content, we expect that we will do a large tuning pass based on our data."

Forever's three launch raids will open December 9, meaning there will be a little over a month without class changes. But launch and its subsequent months will just be the beginning, Blizzard said.

"This is all merely a starting point for the classes in Forever, which will continue over the course of the months and years ahead just as they did following the original launch in 2004," Blizzard said. 

Blizzard is in it for the long haul with Forever, telling GameSpot in an interview it hopes the game will continue to receive updates for the next 10-20 years (or potentially forever). It recently announced its plans to release major Forever content updates every four months, as well as teased how its controller support will eventually lead to players being able to play the MMORPG on "whatever you want." 

WoW: Forever launches November 4, but you can make your character now. In other Forever news, Blizzards revealed it will be making major improvements to the game's divisive layering system, how it's avoiding the problem of "dead" servers, and announced big changes to racial abilities alongside its newly announced class changes.

#3603. Pre-K Teacher's Aide Filmed Himself Assaulting Kids In School: Prosecutors

A teacher’s aide is facing 61 charges after he allegedly filmed himself sexually assaulting multiple children inside the elementary school where he worked.

Shaun M. Stebbins of Somers Point, New Jersey, was previously arrested on March 29 on several charges, including aggravated sexual assault and child sex abuse material offenses in connection with allegations that he abused four children, who are siblings, over a span of several years.

That sexual assault investigation revealed additional alleged crimes involving students at Woodbine Elementary School in Cape May County, the Cape May County Prosecutor’s Office announced in a Thursday, October 30, news release.

Investigators discovered Stebbins, 44 — who worked at the school as a pre-kindergarten aide — allegedly took photos and video of children’s genitalia inside a school bathroom, per court documents obtained by WPVI-TV.

Stebbins also allegedly filmed himself sexually assaulting children in the bathroom and during their scheduled nap time.

Stebbins was charged on October 30 with 29 counts of manufacturing child pornography, five counts of aggravated sexual assault, 13 counts of sexual assault by sexual contact and 14 counts of endangering the welfare of a child, according to prosecutors.

“Children are among our most vulnerable population and we have a responsibility to protect their safety and well-being. Anyone who harms a child will be held accountable through our justice system,” Cape May County Prosecutor Jeffrey H. Sutherland said in an October 30 statement.

Stebbins was hired at Woodbine Elementary School in February 2022 and worked at the school for more than four years and until his arrest earlier this year in the separate child sexual assault case, prosecutors said.

In the other case, Stebbins allegedly sexually assaulted four siblings — all of whom are his extended family members — for over a decade, according to NJ.com.

Woodbine School District Superintendent Adrienne Breitinger previously said in a letter to families that the district immediately sought to replace Stebbins following his March 29 arrest, the outlet reported.

“The safety and well-being of our students remain our highest priority,” Breitinger wrote.

Stebbins attended a virtual court appearance Monday in connection with the alleged crimes against students and was ordered detained ahead of his next court date, which is set for November 4, per WPVI-TV.

Information on his legal counsel or whether he entered a plea wasn’t immediately available.

The Cape May County Prosecutor’s Office encourages anyone with information on Stebbins’ case to contact the office’s special victims unit at (609) 465-1135. Anonymous tips can also be submitted online.

If you or someone you know is experiencing child abuse, call or text Child Help Hotline at 1-800-422-4453.

#3601. WoW: Forever Shamans Are Protesting Class Changes After Being “Completely Ignored”

World of Warcraft: Forever just received a massive batch of class-balance updates ahead of launch that have boosted power across the board, but one group of players isn't happy with the changes: Shamans.

Developer Blizzard recently released Forever's launch patch notes based on feedback and data accumulated during the beta, resulting in a power spike for all classes and major reworks for classes like Paladin and Rogue. Shamans, too, received some significant changes, most notably the removal of a key Elemental specialization ability, Lava Burst, along with any interactions other abilities had with it.

It's that change, and other changes to specialization-specific abilities like Restoration's Riptide and Enhancement's Maelstrom Weapon, that have resulted in the WoW Classic Shaman Discord going into lockdown in protest. The entire server, which has around 80,000 members, has been made read-only, with a message declaring the reason for why it took what it described as such a "drastic measure."

"Community feedback gets completely ignored and class fantasies are getting destroyed," the server declared. "With this we intend to give them [Blizzard] a sign and show them that the community is not [happy] with how they approached our beloved class. Give us back our class and spec identities and fantasies."

While the protest is in regards to class changes in Forever specifically, the server is also home to Shaman discussions as they relate to other "classic" versions of the game as well, including WoW Classic and Mists of Pandaria Classic. As of writing, all of those channels are also locked and set to read-only. 

In a follow-up post, the server went into more detail about its complaints in regards to how Blizzard has approached Forever's Shaman design. It stated its complaints aren't about "damage output." It also made clear the server will re-open "regardless of the outcome," but that it felt like its feedback through "legitimate" channels were being ignored. 

The server then proceeded to list what it viewed as wrong with various ability changes for each Shaman specialization. It additionally called attention to what it called the "hybrid spell power issue," where spell power and intellect gear seems to be better for not only Elemental but also Enhancement, muddying the identity between the two specializations. 

Blizzard has previously said it doesn't want "hybrid" classes that can deal damage and heal, like Shamans, to deal more damage than dedicated DPS classes. Players in the WoW community refer to this idea as the "hybrid tax," something those running the Shaman Discord said they are fine with if it means Shaman class design is improved.

"Truthfully, hybrid tax us all you want if the result is a cohesive class with strong class fantasy elements that are actually represented in our playstyles," it said. 

This isn't the first time a WoW class Discord shut down in protest of how class changes. As pointed out by Wowhead, back in August 2025, the modern WoW Paladin Discord was partially closed in protest of the Retribution specialization's raid performance. In that case, only Retribution-specific channels were locked, and the entire protest lasted less than 24 hours. Blizzard did announce Retribution Paladin buffs shortly after, though it's unclear if those changes came at least in part due to the server protest or not.

How long the WoW Classic Shaman Discord remains in lockdown remains to be seen, but Forever launches November 4. Blizzard recently said it doesn't expect to make any more major class changes for at least another month.

#3599. David Baldacci, John Grisham, and Scott Turow Know How a Story Can End. They Say Losing the Rule of Law to Trump Would Be a “Death Sentence for America”

In July, for the first time in seven years, sitting justices of the US Supreme Court testified at the Capitol. Chief Justice John Roberts has been shy about letting members of the Court answer legislators’ questions, viewing it as a violation of the separation of powers. However, in this case, there was apparently no choice, since the Supreme Court requested millions of dollars to enhance its very own security in the face of sharply growing threats to lower court judges—threats that have grown exponentially over the last decade.

We are all lawyers as well as novelists. We have appeared in court on various matters before both judges and juries, and thus believe that respect for the rule of law is absolutely essential to have any hope for a civilized society. Recent events, like the reasons for justices Elena Kagan and Amy Coney Barrett to testify before Congress, have prompted us to write this, because we want all Americans to understand that we are drawing perilously close to the rule of law becoming optional. For any free and open democracy, not only is that unacceptable, but it is a death sentence for America.

Respect for the rule of law must come from everyone, and it most certainly should come from the highest officeholder in the land. Unfortunately, with the current administration, we have witnessed the exact opposite result.

Donald Trump with Supreme Court Chief Justice John Roberts, and Supreme Court Justices Elena Kagan, Brett Kavanaugh, and Amy Coney Barrett in February 2026.

Consider the fundamental text: The Declaration of Independence, which celebrated its 250th anniversary this year—and established what the framers viewed as the bedrock principles for a just government, starting with the declaration’s most hallowed statement, that all persons are created equal. But the document went on to list many grievances against the tyrannical rule of King George III, including the fact that the king had made “Judges dependent on his Will alone,” because it was solely the king’s grace that decided their continued employment or compensation. In response, our Constitution tried to insulate the federal judiciary from outside influence by providing for lifetime appointments.

But fast-forward to the present day, and President Donald Trump has repeatedly demeaned and insulted judges, variously claiming that a judge’s heritage, religion, or political affiliation can compromise their legal judgement. In February, he flagrantly labeled the members of the Supreme Court who had voted to overrule his tariffs as “fools and lapdogs,” claiming they were “swayed by foreign interests,” and attacking Neil Gorsuch and Coney Barrett, two of the justices he himself had appointed, calling them “an embarrassment to their families.”

Even more egregiously, the Trump administration has gone beyond schoolyard insults to taking actions that actually circumvent the rule of law.

For example, Trump’s use of the Justice Department to bring criminal prosecutions against those he thinks wronged him personally is one of his most brazen acts of defiance of established legal norms. The indictments of former FBI director James Comey, whom Trump fired, and Letitia James, the New York attorney general who brought a successful civil fraud case against Trump, his children, and Trump family businesses, were both thrown out of court because Trump’s selection of one of his former personal lawyers as the prosecutor was found illegal. The newest prosecution of Comey, because of a supposedly threatening arrangement of seashells on a beach, is equally unlikely to stand up under prevailing law.

The Ábrego Garcia matter is another instance of abuse, because it dramatizes the disobedience by the Trump administration with respect to immigration court orders. Kilmar Armando Ábrego Garcia was deported to the Salvadorean mega-prison despite being legally present in the US. The government first refused to return him, claiming, without adequate proof, that he was a member of the criminal organization MS-13. However, once the pressure became too much, he was returned to the US. Only then did the Justice Department charge him with human smuggling, claiming he had transported people within the US who were in the country unlawfully. His case was dismissed by the trial judge on the grounds of vindictive and selective prosecution and remains on appeal.

We are, without a doubt, in the midst of a veritable plague of looming dangers aimed squarely at the judiciary. Not only did an armed man attempt to assassinate Justice Brett Kavanaugh at his home in 2022 following a leak of the Dobbs decision, hostile threats directed at judges have more than tripled over the past decade, according to Chief Justice Roberts’s 2024 year-end report. Citing statistics from the US Marshals Service, the report said that in the past five years alone, more than 1,000 serious threats were investigated, and dozens of people were charged with crimes. In 2020, the US Marshals said it responded to over 4,000 threats or inappropriate communications against federal judges. In that same year, a disgruntled lawyer murdered US District Judge Esther Salas’s son and wounded her husband after gaining access to their home by posing as a delivery person. According to NBC News, in 2025, there were 103 unordered pizza deliveries to judges who had ruled against the Trump administration or spoke out about threats against the judiciary, and 20 were sent in Salas’s name.

As novelists, for decades, we have all explored themes of corruption, influence peddling, and pressure and threats against public servants in our fiction.

In Scott’s latest novel, Presumed Guilty, about a murder trial in a rural area in the upper Midwest, the longtime prosecutor, Hiram Jackdorp, and the trial judge, Wendy Carrington, have a contentious relationship. Jackdorp forced her out of his office when she was a young prosecutor, and later unsuccessfully attempted to prevent her election to the bench. But there is no moment during the trial when the novel’s narrator, the defense lawyer Rusty Sabich, sees Judge Carrington’s rulings as based on anything but a fair application of legal principles. She is a good judge whose fidelity to the rule of law prevents her from using her position for personal revenge.

In John’s 2008 novel The Appeal, an ambitious young attorney is unwittingly recruited by some nefarious special interests to seek election to the state supreme court. Their big money pours in and buys enough votes. He wins, unseats a legendary jurist, and takes office. But when the pay-off comes due, he realizes that his judicial independence is far more important than playing politics.

In David’s 1996 novel Absolute Power, an American president presumes himself to be above the rule of law and seeks to force his underlings to commit criminal acts that will benefit him. However, the institutions created to check and prevent just such abuses hold fast against these brazen king-like attempts to be immune from baldly unlawful actions. At the end of the novel the truth is revealed, and the criminal justice system holds the president appropriately accountable for his misdeeds.

The “rule of law” is not simply a slogan the three of us learned in law school, or a plot device we use in our fiction. It is what keeps our life in society from turning into the war of all against all, where laws that allow for a civilized way of life matter little and violence and chaos reign. It’s also what keeps our economy vibrant and growing.

Without the fair enforcement of the laws being sacrosanct, economic decline inevitably follows as investors decide against investing in American businesses, building plants or factories here, or purchasing American corporate or government bonds and other investment vehicles. If there is no certainty that commercial contracts or international trade agreements will be honored, this will also vastly diminish the potential of any economy. And if the environment is one where an unbiased court is not the final arbiter of legal disputes, our allies may well think twice before committing resources and lasting cooperation since the environment they sought to work and invest within could change without regard to legality. Economic decline invariably leads to widespread job losses, a lessening standard of living, a loss of confidence in institutions by the citizens, our allies stampeding away from us, and a dilution of every individual right outlined in the Constitution.

And it’s not just us who are worried. There are many other lawyers and judges who have expressed concern about the trajectory of this country to ignore court rulings if they collide with political expediency or partisan goals. Nonpartisan organizations like Keep Our Republic’s Article III Coalition initiative and the Democracy Rising Collaborative have brought together retired judges and advocates to sound the alarm over a country in peril.

What we are all advocating for is that the courts be given the respect they are due under the founding documents of this country. Article I of the United States Constitution established the legislative branch, the United States Congress. Article II established the executive branch, headed up by the presidency. Article III created the US Supreme Court, and granted the power to Congress to establish lower federal courts.

In the 1803 ruling of Marbury v. Madison, the Supreme Court asserted that the courts had the power of judicial review, and with that power came the ability to declare laws passed by the Congress as being unconstitutional. This one ruling lifted the judicial branch to full equality with the other branches, because their decisions would constitute the final ruling on whether or not something was legal or constitutional and in agreement with our rights protected under the Constitution.

In order to be fair and objective arbiters of the law, federal courts must be free from influence, bias, and manipulation from outside sources. There can be no middle ground here. The courts are either free to do their work or they are not.

Each time a court order is ignored or defied, a sliver of independence is torn from the judicial robe. If the executive branch’s answer to a ruling it does not like is simply to not enforce it, or to encourage disobedience through open disrespect, then the independence of the judiciary evaporates. Not only does the legal system itself suffer from this noncompliance, but every citizen does as well, because if one branch of government can defy and ignore court decisions, that means they can potentially defy and ignore the individual rights of any American citizen.

The rule of law must be respected, and the valid decisions of courts must be upheld by the government, even, and perhaps most importantly, when that ruling goes against the government. Only in that way can a free and independent judiciary continue to deliver the ideals outlined in the founding documents of what is the most durable democracy ever conceived and created. Without that, America can no longer claim to be the shining beacon on the hill, inspiring democracy the world over. We, in fact, will become the opposite of what this country has always stood for. Even with our combined imaginations, we can envision no greater tragedy.
